Fact.Name: Qualified solar electric property costs (Form 5695 line 1)
Fact.Description: Costs of property that uses solar energy to generate electricity for use in a home located in the United States (need not be the main home), including labor costs for onsite preparation, assembly, or original installation and for piping or wiring to interconnect the property to the home. Total across homes if more than one. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the property's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableSolarElectricNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695SolarElectricCostTakenIntoAccount). Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ treated as 0 on line 6a. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed; for a reconstructed home, when your original use of it begins; for a newly constructed home, when your original use of it begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here.

Fact.Name: Qualified solar water heating property costs (Form 5695 line 2)
Fact.Description: Costs of property to heat water for use in a home located in the United States if at least half of the energy used by the property for such purpose is derived from the sun; must be certified by the Solar Rating Certification Corporation or a comparable state-endorsed entity. Includes allocable labor costs. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Exclude any cost allocable to a swimming pool, hot tub, or other energy storage medium serving a function other than heating water for the home (§25D(e)(3)). Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the property's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableSolarWaterHeatingNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695SolarWaterHeatingCostTakenIntoAccount). Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ treated as 0 on line 6a. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed; for a reconstructed home, when your original use of it begins; for a newly constructed home, when your original use of it begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here.

Fact.Name: Qualified small wind energy property costs (Form 5695 line 3)
Fact.Description: Costs of property that uses a wind turbine to generate electricity for use in connection with a home located in the United States. Includes allocable labor costs. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the property's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableSmallWindEnergyNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695SmallWindEnergyCostTakenIntoAccount). Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ treated as 0 on line 6a. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed; for a reconstructed home, when your original use of it begins; for a newly constructed home, when your original use of it begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here.

Fact.Name: Qualified geothermal heat pump property costs (Form 5695 line 4)
Fact.Description: Costs of equipment that uses the ground or ground water as a thermal energy source to heat, or as a thermal energy sink to cool, a home located in the United States; must meet Energy Star program requirements in effect at purchase. Includes allocable labor costs. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the property's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableGeothermalHeatPumpNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695GeothermalHeatPumpCostTakenIntoAccount). Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ treated as 0 on line 6a. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed; for a reconstructed home, when your original use of it begins; for a newly constructed home, when your original use of it begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here.

Fact.Name: Battery storage technology has a capacity of at least 3 kilowatt hours (Form 5695 line 5a)
Fact.Description: Whether the qualified battery storage technology has a capacity of at least 3 kilowatt hours. If No, no credit may be claimed for battery storage technology costs and line 5b adds nothing to line 6a; unanswered while a battery cost is entered, the return is held (/form5695Line5aAnsweredWhenBatteryCostEntered; tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Qualified battery storage technology costs (Form 5695 line 5b)
Fact.Description: Costs of battery storage technology installed in connection with a home located in the United States with a capacity of at least 3 kilowatt hours. Counted on line 6a only if /writableBatteryStorageAtLeast3kwh is Yes. Includes allocable labor costs. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Exclude any cost allocable to a swimming pool, hot tub, or other energy storage medium serving a function other than storing electricity for the home (§25D(e)(3)). Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the property's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableBatteryStorageNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695BatteryStorageCostTakenIntoAccount). Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ treated as 0 on line 6a. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed; for a reconstructed home, when your original use of it begins; for a newly constructed home, when your original use of it begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here.

Fact.Name: Total qualified residential clean energy property costs (Form 5695 line 6a)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 6a = lines 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5b, where line 5b counts only if the battery storage capacity question (line 5a) is Yes. Each unanswered cost line is treated as 0; a line 5b cost with line 5a unanswered leaves this line unresolved and holds the return (/form5695Line5aAnsweredWhenBatteryCostEntered, IN-277). A line whose per-item list is supplied counts as answered, so its items reach line 6a (a list whose items do not add up to the line's whole cost leaves line 6a unresolved rather than $0) (FED-5695-NONBUSINESS80-013).

Fact.Name: Tentative residential clean energy credit, 30% of costs (Form 5695 line 6b)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 6b = 30% × line 6a. One of the three addends of line 13 (/form5695Line13TotalCredit, "Add lines 6b, 11, and 12"), the amount the line 14/15 limit chain is applied to.

Fact.Name: Residential Clean Energy Credit Limit Worksheet line 2 (credits ordered before this credit)
Fact.Description: Worksheet line 2: the total of the credits/adjustments taken on the 2025 return that are applied against tax BEFORE the residential clean energy credit — Schedule 3 line 6l, the foreign tax credit (Schedule 3 line 1), the child and dependent care credit (Schedule 3 line 2), the credit for the elderly or disabled (Schedule 3 line 6d), nonrefundable education credits (Schedule 3 line 3), the retirement savings contributions credit (Schedule 3 line 4), the energy efficient home improvement credit (Form 5695 line 32 → Schedule 3 line 5b), clean vehicle credits (Schedule 3 lines 6f and 6m), the mortgage interest credit (Schedule 3 line 6g, Form 8396 line 9), the adoption credit (Schedule 3 line 6c, Form 8839 line 18), the DC first-time homebuyer credit carryforward (Schedule 3 line 6h, collected by dictionary/ty2025/form8859.xml; complete-safe 0 wherever the carryforward is unanswered), and the CTC/ODC (Form 1040 line 19). This fact is the PLAIN ARM of a two-arm chain. Its twin, /form5695CreditLimitWorksheetLine2Wsb, applies the CTC/ODC term's Credit Limit Worksheet B footnote (Worksheet B line 14 in place of Form 1040 line 19, plus the 6g and 6c TWINS in place of Schedule 3's public lines, and schedule3:/sched3Line6h subtracted on this plain arm against form8859's Worksheet-B twin subtracted on the twin arm), and /residentialCleanEnergyCredit selects between the two on ctcOdc:/isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB. The CTC/ODC term's own footnote (i5695 worksheet line 2 footnote, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i5695.pdf, page 5): "Include the amount in the instructions for Schedule 8812 (Form 1040), Credit Limit Worksheet B, line 14, INSTEAD of the amount from Form 1040 ... line 19, if the instructions for Schedule 8812 direct you to complete Credit Limit Worksheet B." This plain arm reads the CTC/ODC term from /totalCtcAndOdc (Form 1040 line 19). When the filer completes Credit Limit Worksheet B the twin arm applies, reading ctcOdc:/sched8812CreditLimitWorksheetBLine14 in its place, and ctcOdc's own Credit Limit Worksheet A line 4 reads /sched8812CreditLimitWorksheetBLine15, so both legs of Worksheet B are carried by the twin facts. Non-circular (VERIFIED MECHANICALLY, not by grep — scripts/factdag.py up /sched3Line6c): the entire upstream cone of the 6c term contains no Part I fact of this module and no Schedule 3 line 5a. Form 8839's own Credit Limit Worksheet (line 3) enumerates Schedule 3 lines 1-4, 5b, 6d, 6f, 6g, 6l, 6m — 5a and 6c both excluded — so 5a → 6c → … never loops back to 5a. Likewise ctcOdc /sched8812CreditLimit enumerates lines 1/2/3/4/5b/6d/6f/6l/6m (5a and 6c both excluded), and the 6g credit's own Credit Limit Worksheet also excludes 5a.

Fact.Name: Residential Clean Energy Credit Limit Worksheet line 2 — the Credit Limit Worksheet B twin
Fact.Description:
/form5695CreditLimitWorksheetLine2 with THREE substitutions, all forced by the same rule: * the Form 1040 line 19 (CTC/ODC) term becomes ctcOdc:/sched8812CreditLimitWorksheetBLine14 — the asterisk footnote this module's plain twin quotes at i5695 lines 381-385 and, until this build, declined to model; * the Schedule 3 line 6g term becomes form8396:/mortgageInterestCreditWsb; * the Schedule 3 line 6c term becomes form8839:/nonrefundableAdoptionCreditWsb. The last two are not bookkeeping. A filer completing Worksheet B figures Form 8396 and Form 8839 under the SAME substitution — each of those worksheets carries the identical printed footnote — so the 6g and 6c amounts that belong in this list are the twins'. Mechanically, reading /sched3Line6g or /sched3Line6c here would reach the PUBLIC selectors, whose plain arms read /totalCtcAndOdc, which after step 5 is downstream of this credit: a cycle that parks the dictionary load at 0% CPU with no error.
Both arms of this worksheet enumerate every term the IRS prints on it: this twin arm subtracts form8859:/dcFirstTimeHomebuyerCreditWsb (the Form 8859 District of Columbia first-time homebuyer credit, Worksheet-B twin) and the plain arm subtracts schedule3:/sched3Line6h, one printed term each, with Worksheet B line 15 carrying the matching fourth addend. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE; whole dollars, where the plain twin already puts them.

Fact.Name: Limitation based on tax liability (Form 5695 line 14) — the Credit Limit Worksheet B twin
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 14 on the Worksheet B arm: Form 1040 line 18 minus /form5695CreditLimitWorksheetLine2Wsb, floored at 0. Identical shape to the plain arm; only the subtrahend differs.

Fact.Name: Residential clean energy credit — the Credit Limit Worksheet B twin (Form 5695 line 15)
Fact.Description:
Form 5695 line 15 on the Worksheet B arm = smaller of line 13 (/form5695Line13TotalCredit, "Add lines 6b, 11, and 12") and the twin line-14 limit. This is the value Credit Limit Worksheet B line 15 takes for Schedule 3 line 5a, and the value the public /residentialCleanEnergyCredit selects when the filer is completing Worksheet B.
NOT ITSELF GATED ON THE TRIGGER, for the reason form8396's twin states: the selector owns that choice, so this fact can be read by /sched8812CreditLimit's chain (step 5) without dragging the trigger, and hence the public credit paths, into that cone. It keeps the SAME /residentialCleanEnergyPartIIsActive branch gate, so a return with no Part I cost line answered takes the else-0 branch without evaluating the limit chain.

Fact.Name: Limitation based on tax liability (Form 5695 line 14)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 14, from the Residential Clean Energy Credit Limit Worksheet: line 1 (Form 1040 line 18, taxCalculations /totalTentativeTax) minus line 2 (the credits ordered before this credit), floored at 0 ("If zero or less, enter -0- on Form 5695, lines 14 and 15").

Fact.Name: Return has Form 5695 Part I (residential clean energy) input
Fact.Description: True when any Form 5695 Part I cost or carryforward line is answered (the five line 1-5 cost categories, the line 8 fuel cell cost, the line 12 carryforward from 2024), a Part I item list is supplied, or the line 7c worksheet applies. A VALUE-PRESERVING EXTRACTION of the branch gate that /residentialCleanEnergyCredit already carried inline (the pattern), now named so a second consumer can read it. THE SECOND CONSUMER IS WHY THIS EXISTS: ctcOdc:/isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB needs Credit Limit Worksheet A line 3's "you are claiming ... c. Residential clean energy credit, Form 5695, Part I" limb, and it must read an INPUT gate rather than the credit VALUE. That trigger is the When of the public bridge-credit selectors, so reading /residentialCleanEnergyCredit there would make each selector depend on the quantity it selects, and the resolver builds every Switch branch eagerly — the cycle would park the dictionary load at 0% CPU rather than raise. It reads the Part I cost and carryforward writables, the six Part I item-list selections (/form5695Line{1,2,3,4,5b,8}*ItemsSelected) and the line 7c worksheet selection (/form5695FuelCellJointWorksheetSelected, which reads the filing status); none of these reads a credit value. Part II (the energy efficient home improvement credit, Schedule 3 line 5b) is deliberately NOT in this test: Worksheet A line 3 names Form 5695 PART I only, and Part II's credit is ordered before both the CTC and Part I rather than after them. WHAT IS COUNTED (tax interpretation IN-277 (k)): a line 5b cost or item list behind a No on line 5a, and a line 8 cost, item list or joint worksheet behind a No on line 7a, is not taken into account, so it does not make Part I active; with nothing else counted, Part I is not active and Form 5695 is not required by Part I.

Fact.Name: Residential clean energy credit (Form 5695 line 15 → Schedule 3 line 5a)
Fact.Description:
Form 5695 line 15 = smaller of line 13 (/form5695Line13TotalCredit, "Add lines 6b, 11, and 12") and line 14 (/form5695TaxLiabilityLimit). Nonrefundable; flows to Schedule 3 line 5a → /line8OfSchedule3 → Form 1040 line 20. Any excess of line 13 over line 15 is the line 16 carryforward to 2026 (/form5695Line16CarryforwardTo2026; print only, multi-year state not modeled). Complete-safe: with no Part I cost or carryforward line answered, the else branch yields 0 without evaluating the line 14 limit chain (so prior scenarios keep /line8OfSchedule3 byte-identical even where their CTC/tax facts are Placeholder or Incomplete).
This fact is a selector over two arms. The FIRST Case asks ctcOdc:/isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB — Credit Limit Worksheet A line 3's trigger — and returns /residentialCleanEnergyCreditWsb, the twin whose line-14 limit applies the CTC/ODC term's Credit Limit Worksheet B footnote (quoted at /form5695CreditLimitWorksheetLine2). This fact is strictly DOWNSTREAM of both arms and neither arm reads this path, which is what lets /sched8812CreditLimit read the twin without closing a cycle.
On the whole corpus the Worksheet B trigger is Complete-FALSE on every baseline case, so the first Case is never taken there and those scenarios keep /sched3Line5a, /line8OfSchedule3 and total tax byte-identical. BASIS: the increase in the basis of the home that the expenditures would otherwise produce is reduced by the amount of this credit allowed. That reduction changes no amount on this year's return; it matters when the home is later sold, so the filer keeps a record of the credit with the home's basis records.

Fact.Name: Qualified energy efficiency improvements installed in or on your main home in the United States (Form 5695 line 17a)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 17a. If No, the energy efficient home improvement credit cannot be claimed for Section A qualified energy efficiency improvements (lines 18-20); Section B has its own gates (lines 21a/21b). Following the form text ("Do not complete Part II, Section A") over the broader instruction phrasing — see the module header. Unanswered while a Section A cost is entered, the return is held and the Section A lines do not resolve (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered; tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Original user of the qualified energy efficiency improvements (Form 5695 line 17b)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 17b. If No, Section A is excluded (its lines are $0) (original use of the component must begin with the taxpayer). Unanswered while a Section A cost is entered, the return is held and the Section A lines do not resolve (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered; tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Components reasonably expected to remain in use for at least 5 years (Form 5695 line 17c)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 17c. If No, Section A is excluded (its lines are $0). Unanswered while a Section A cost is entered, the return is held and the Section A lines do not resolve (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered; tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Improvements related to the construction of the main home (Form 5695 line 17e)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 17e. If Yes, lines 18a through 20d are skipped ("You cannot claim the credit for expenses related to the construction of a new home"). Section A counts only when this is answered No; with Yes the Section A lines are $0; with it unanswered while a Section A cost is entered, the return is held and the Section A lines do not resolve (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered; tax interpretations IN-277, IN-278). HOW TO ANSWER: No when the improvements you are claiming are improvements to an existing home, or an addition to or renovation of one, even if the home also had construction-related improvements you are not claiming (leave those out of lines 18a through 20d); Yes only when the improvements you would claim are related to the construction of a new home.

Fact.Name: Part II Section A available (lines 17a Yes, 17b Yes, 17c Yes, 17e No)
Fact.Description: Whether the Section A qualified-energy-efficiency-improvement lines (18-20) may be completed: lines 17a/17b/17c each answered Yes and line 17e answered No. Unanswered gates ⇒ false (and with a Section A cost entered the return is held through /form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered, IN-277) (complete-safe on every scenario without Part II entries). Reading: a No on 17a/b/c bars only Section A ("Do not complete Part II, Section A" — the form's own scope), not Section B, which the form gates separately at 21a/21b.

Fact.Name: Insulation or air sealing material or system costs (Form 5695 line 18a)
Fact.Description: Cost of insulation material or system (including air sealing material or system, vapor retarders, seals to limit infiltration) specifically and primarily designed to reduce heat loss or gain of the home, meeting the IECC criteria (as in effect January 1, 2021). Building envelope component: do NOT include onsite preparation/assembly/installation labor. No QMID line on the form (insulation is not specified property). Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing — financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or -production projects (§25C(f)(3)). Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the property's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableInsulationNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1) importing §25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695InsulationCostTakenIntoAccount). Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ 0. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here.

Fact.Name: Cost of the most expensive qualifying exterior door (Form 5695 line 19a)
Fact.Description: Cost of the most expensive exterior door bought that meets the applicable Energy Star requirements. No installation labor. The $250 per-door credit cap (line 19c) applies to this door; remaining doors go on /writableOtherDoorCosts. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing — financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or -production projects (§25C(f)(3)). Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the property's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableMostExpensiveDoorNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1) importing §25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695MostExpensiveDoorCostTakenIntoAccount). Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ 0. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here.

Fact.Name: Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number for the exterior doors (Form 5695 line 19b)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 19b, the four-character alphanumeric QMID of the most expensive door on line 19a (letters and digits only, exactly four; a longer entry is rejected). It gates line 19a only: without it the line 19a cost counts $0 (section 25C(h)(1)(B); tax interpretation IN-271). The doors on lines 19d(i)-(ii) are gated by their own first-four boxes, and the line 19e doors by each statement item's QMID. The last 13 characters of the printed identifier go in /writableLine19bQmidLast13.

Fact.Name: Cost of all other qualifying exterior doors (Form 5695 line 19f = lines 19d + 19e)
Fact.Description: Combined cost of the qualifying exterior doors other than the most expensive one — the form's line 19d (two next most expensive, itemized with QMIDs) plus line 19e (all others, QMIDs on an attached statement), typed as one line 19f total; the itemized lines 19d and 19e are what the computation reads. No installation labor. A typed total here carries no per-door QMID, so it adds $0 (see EARNS NO CREDIT). Itemize each additional door on line 19d with its own QMID (/writableLine19dEntry1Cost with /writableLine19dEntry1QmidFirst4, /writableLine19dEntry2Cost with /writableLine19dEntry2QmidFirst4) or on the line 19e statement. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing — financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or -production projects (§25C(f)(3)). Enter the whole cost. Its nonbusiness-use percentage is not asked: a typed total adds $0, so no allocation is owed for it. Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ 0. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. EARNS NO CREDIT: an amount entered here names no item's QMID, and section 25C(h)(1) allows the credit only for an item whose own QMID is on the return, so it adds $0 to the credit. Itemize each item with its QMID on the printed line or the attached statement instead.

Fact.Name: Costs of exterior windows and skylights (Form 5695 line 20c = lines 20a + 20b)
Fact.Description: Combined cost of all exterior windows and skylights that meet the Energy Star certification requirements — the form's line 20a (four most expensive, itemized with QMIDs) plus line 20b (all others, QMIDs on an attached statement), typed as one total; the computation reads the itemized lines 20a and the line 20b statement, not this total. No installation labor. A typed total here carries no per-window QMID, and section 25C(h)(1) allows the credit only for an item whose QMID is reported, so a typed total adds $0 to line 20d (see EARNS NO CREDIT). Itemize each window on line 20a with its own QMID to report the detail the statute asks for. Enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf (i5695 Caution, p.1). Exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing — financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or -production projects (§25C(f)(3)). Enter the whole cost. Its nonbusiness-use percentage is not asked: a typed total adds $0, so no allocation is owed for it. Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ 0. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. EARNS NO CREDIT: an amount entered here names no item's QMID, and section 25C(h)(1) allows the credit only for an item whose own QMID is on the return, so it adds $0 to the credit. Itemize each item with its QMID on the printed line or the attached statement instead.

Fact.Name: Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number for the windows/skylights (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: Retired category-level QMID intake for the windows and skylights on line 20a; it gates nothing (see NO LONGER A GATE). Enter the four-character alphanumeric QMID printed by the manufacturer: four characters exactly, letters and digits only, and a longer entry is rejected. The remaining 13 characters of the printed identifier belong in the second box of the printed line, /writableLine20aEntry1QmidLast13, never here. NO LONGER A GATE (FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048, FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046): this unprinted category-level intake is not read by any credit. Fact.Name: Insulation/air sealing credit, 30% capped at $1,200 (Form 5695 line 18b)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 18b = 30% × line 18a, not more than $1,200. Counts only when Section A is available (lines 17a-17e) and line 18a is answered; else 0 (complete-safe). Whole-dollar HALF_UP rounding on the multiplication. No QMID requirement (insulation is not specified property). JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): the credit allocable to you for this property is the smaller of line 18b as usually figured (/form5695InsulationCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and the property's credit limit ($1,200) times the amount you paid (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidInsulation) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidInsulation plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidInsulationOrZero), rounded to whole dollars. That is the instructions' rule: when the aggregate credit for all occupants exceeds the limit, your share is the limit times your fraction; when it does not, the usual figure is already the smaller. With line 32a checked and the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Credit for the most expensive exterior door, 30% capped at $250 (Form 5695 line 19c)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 19c applies the individual 250 dollar cap and, where applicable, the same-door joint payment fraction using exact hidden arithmetic. Round the printed line once to whole dollars; its separately retained exact contribution enters line 19h.

Fact.Name: Credit for the other exterior doors, 30% uncapped per-line (Form 5695 line 19g)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 19g is 30 percent of qualifying other-door costs on line 19f, rounded once to whole dollars. This is the raw printed multiplication for both printed and statement routes. Every physical door receives its own statutory 250 dollar cap in line 19h, independently of this printed subtotal. A selected statement must be complete and reconciled; closed Section A contributes zero and an unanswered required section question remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Exterior door credit, all doors, capped at $500 (Form 5695 line 19h)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 19h applies the 250 dollar limit to each qualifying physical door before the 500 dollar all-door ceiling, regardless of ordering or use adjustments. Under joint occupancy, sum exact same-door allocations; apply the household payment-share ceiling only when the exact sum of household item-capped credits exceeds 500 dollars. Retain arbitrary-precision fractions through all hidden operations and round the final line once. The household inventory includes doors paid entirely by others. Missing or contradictory required information holds the return. When Section A is closed by its eligibility answers, the door credit is zero without reading the unused statement or joint-allocation details.

Fact.Name: Window and skylight credit, 30% capped at $600 (Form 5695 line 20d)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 20d = 30% × line 20c, not more than $600 (combined limit for all exterior windows and skylights). Counts only when Section A is available, the window costs are answered, and each window counts only with its own printed QMID (tax interpretation IN-271); else 0. When /form5695Line20bOtherWindowItems is selected, its independently identified item costs and reconciliation control this credit. No category-header QMID substitutes for a missing item QMID, and a header is not required for an unused printed item. Existing dollar ceilings remain. Without a statement (item list), the line b amount is $0: a typed line b amount or a typed category total names no item's QMID and adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271; owner ruling NE-6). QMID RULE: each item's own QMID is checked on its printed line, where an item without one already counts $0, so this line no longer requires an unprinted category-header QMID (FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046, FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048). JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): the credit allocable to you for this property is the smaller of line 20d as usually figured (/form5695WindowCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and the property's credit limit ($600) times the amount you paid (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidWindowsSkylights) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidWindowsSkylights plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidWindowsSkylightsOrZero), rounded to whole dollars. That is the instructions' rule: when the aggregate credit for all occupants exceeds the limit, your share is the limit times your fraction; when it does not, the usual figure is already the smaller. With line 32a checked and the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Central air conditioner credit, 30% capped at $600 (Form 5695 line 22d)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 22d = 30% × line 22c, not more than $600. Counts only when Section B is available (21a/21b Yes), the cost is answered, and each item counts only with its own printed QMID (tax interpretation IN-271); else 0. When /form5695Line22bOtherCentralAcItems is selected, its independently identified item costs and reconciliation control this credit. No category-header QMID substitutes for a missing item QMID, and a header is not required for an unused printed item. Existing dollar ceilings remain. Without a statement (item list), the line b amount is $0: a typed line b amount or a typed category total names no item's QMID and adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271; owner ruling NE-6). QMID RULE: each item's own QMID is checked on its printed line, where an item without one already counts $0, so this line no longer requires an unprinted category-header QMID (FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046, FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048). JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): the credit allocable to you for this property is the smaller of line 22d as usually figured (/form5695CentralAcCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and the property's credit limit ($600) times the amount you paid (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidCentralAirConditioners) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidCentralAirConditioners plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidCentralAirConditionersOrZero), rounded to whole dollars. That is the instructions' rule: when the aggregate credit for all occupants exceeds the limit, your share is the limit times your fraction; when it does not, the usual figure is already the smaller. With line 32a checked and the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Natural gas/propane/oil water heater credit, 30% capped at $600 (Form 5695 line 23d)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 23d = 30% × line 23c, not more than $600. Section B gate + cost; each item counts only with its own printed QMID (tax interpretation IN-271); else 0. When /form5695Line23bOtherWaterHeaterItems is selected, its independently identified item costs and reconciliation control this credit. No category-header QMID substitutes for a missing item QMID, and a header is not required for an unused printed item. Existing dollar ceilings remain. Without a statement (item list), the line b amount is $0: a typed line b amount or a typed category total names no item's QMID and adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271; owner ruling NE-6). QMID RULE: each item's own QMID is checked on its printed line, where an item without one already counts $0, so this line no longer requires an unprinted category-header QMID (FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046, FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048). JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): the credit allocable to you for this property is the smaller of line 23d as usually figured (/form5695FossilFuelWaterHeaterCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and the property's credit limit ($600) times the amount you paid (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidWaterHeaters) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidWaterHeaters plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidWaterHeatersOrZero), rounded to whole dollars. That is the instructions' rule: when the aggregate credit for all occupants exceeds the limit, your share is the limit times your fraction; when it does not, the usual figure is already the smaller. With line 32a checked and the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Furnace/hot water boiler credit, 30% capped at $600 (Form 5695 line 24d)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 24d = 30% × line 24c, not more than $600. Section B gate + cost; each item counts only with its own printed QMID (tax interpretation IN-271); else 0. When /form5695Line24bOtherFurnaceBoilerItems is selected, its independently identified item costs and reconciliation control this credit. No category-header QMID substitutes for a missing item QMID, and a header is not required for an unused printed item. Existing dollar ceilings remain. Without a statement (item list), the line b amount is $0: a typed line b amount or a typed category total names no item's QMID and adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271; owner ruling NE-6). QMID RULE: each item's own QMID is checked on its printed line, where an item without one already counts $0, so this line no longer requires an unprinted category-header QMID (FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046, FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048). JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): the credit allocable to you for this property is the smaller of line 24d as usually figured (/form5695FurnaceBoilerCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and the property's credit limit ($600) times the amount you paid (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidFurnacesBoilers) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidFurnacesBoilers plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidFurnacesBoilersOrZero), rounded to whole dollars. That is the instructions' rule: when the aggregate credit for all occupants exceeds the limit, your share is the limit times your fraction; when it does not, the usual figure is already the smaller. With line 32a checked and the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Enabling property credit, 30% capped at $600 (Form 5695 line 25e)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 25e = 30% × line 25c, not more than $600. Section B gate + line 25a answered Yes + cost + the line 25d QMID; else 0. Line 25e is 30% of the printed line 25c (/form5695EnablingPropertyCostTakenIntoAccount), which already carries the enabled-property rule: line 25c is $0 when the line 25b codes name only energy property for which no credit is allowed, and is $0 when line 25a is Yes but no line 25b code is entered (FED-5695-P2-25BCODES-031). JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): the credit allocable to you for this property is the smaller of line 25e as usually figured (/form5695EnablingPropertyCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and the property's credit limit ($600) times the amount you paid (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidEnablingProperty) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidEnablingProperty plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidEnablingPropertyOrZero), rounded to whole dollars. That is the instructions' rule: when the aggregate credit for all occupants exceeds the limit, your share is the limit times your fraction; when it does not, the usual figure is already the smaller. With line 32a checked and the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: A Form 5695 line 25b enabled-property code is entered
Fact.Description: True when at least one of the seven line 25b code boxes (/writableLine25bEnabledPropertyCode1 through 7) is answered. The form requires a code when line 25a is answered Yes, so with line 25a Yes and an enabling property cost but no code, the printed line 25c, and so the line 25e credit, is $0 (FED-5695-P2-25BCODES-031).

Fact.Name: The enabled property named on Form 5695 line 25b qualifies the enabling property
Fact.Description: True when a line 25b code names enabled property that the enabling property was installed in conjunction with, as section 25C(d)(2)(D)(iii) requires: code A (windows and skylights reported on line 20a) is a qualified energy efficiency improvement, for which the statute requires no allowed credit, but it counts only when a window or skylight is reported on line 20a and taken into account on this return: Section A not closed by an answer (17a-17c Yes, 17e No) and the line 20a amount (/form5695Line20aWindowCost) above $0. With Section A closed, or no qualifying line 20a window, code A qualifies nothing, so line 25c, line 25e and the line 28 numerator take no enabling cost on it; while Section A waits on an unanswered line 17 question with a window cost entered, this does not resolve (tax interpretation IN-272, code A addition); codes B through G name qualified energy property, which counts only when a credit is allowed for it on this return: B the central air conditioner credit on line 22d, C the water heater credit on line 23d, D the furnace or boiler credit on line 24d, and E, F and G a heat pump, heat pump water heater or biomass cost on line 29 with a line 29h credit above $0. A code B-G whose enabled property earns no credit does not qualify the enabling property, and the printed line 25c, and so line 25e, is then $0 (FED-5695-P2-25BCODES-031).

Fact.Name: Home energy audit credit, 30% capped at $150 (Form 5695 line 26c)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 26c = 30% × line 26b, not more than $150. Gated ONLY on line 26a (answered Yes) and the cost being answered — NOT on the Section B 21a/21b gates (the form's 21 skip text routes directly to line 26) and NOT on the Section A 17 gates (audits are neither a building envelope component nor qualified energy property). No QMID. JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): the credit allocable to you for this property is the smaller of line 26c as usually figured (/form5695HomeEnergyAuditCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and the property's credit limit ($150) times the amount you paid (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidHomeEnergyAudits) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidHomeEnergyAudits plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidHomeEnergyAuditsOrZero), rounded to whole dollars. That is the instructions' rule: when the aggregate credit for all occupants exceeds the limit, your share is the limit times your fraction; when it does not, the usual figure is already the smaller. With line 32a checked and the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Sum of the $1,200-bucket per-item credits (Form 5695 line 27)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 27 = lines 18b + 19h + 20d + 22d + 23d + 24d + 25e + 26c. Every term is complete-safe 0, so this resolves 0 on any return without Part II entries.

Fact.Name: Combined credit after the $1,200 annual cap (Form 5695 line 28)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 28 = smaller of line 27 or $1,200 — the total combined annual credit limit for qualified energy efficiency improvements, energy property, and audits. The line 29 heat pump / biomass bucket sits OUTSIDE this cap. JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): when line 27 is more than $1,200, line 28 is $1,200 times the sum of the amounts you paid on lines 18a, 19a, 19f, 20a, 20b, 22a, 22b, 23a, 23b, 24a, 24b, 25c and 26b (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidLine28Properties) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants for the corresponding properties (that sum plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidLine28Properties), rounded to whole dollars; otherwise line 28 is figured as usual (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Heat pump, heat pump water heater, and biomass stove/boiler costs (Form 5695 line 29g)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 29g = lines 29a through 29f — the three derived category amounts /form5695Line29HeatPumpCosts (29a + 29b), /form5695Line29HeatPumpWaterHeaterCosts (29c + 29d) and /form5695Line29BiomassCosts (29e + 29f), each figured from its printed item lines and its line b statement (a typed category total adds $0, tax interpretation IN-271), each counted only when Section B is available, each item only with its own printed QMID (tax interpretation IN-271) ($0 for a category with no item). It does not resolve while a Section B cost waits on an unanswered line 21 question (IN-277). QMID RULE: each item's own QMID is checked on its printed line, where an item without one already counts $0, so this line no longer requires an unprinted category-header QMID (FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046, FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section B cost waits on an unanswered line 21 question (/form5695SectionBQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section B is closed by an answer.

Fact.Name: Heat pump / heat pump water heater / biomass credit, 30% capped at $2,000 (Form 5695 line 29h)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 29h = 30% × line 29g, not more than $2,000 — the separate annual limit for heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, and biomass stoves/boilers, OUTSIDE the $1,200 combined cap. Whole-dollar HALF_UP rounding on the multiplication. JOINT OCCUPANTS (line 32a checked): line 29h is the smaller of its usual figure (/form5695HeatPumpBiomassCreditBeforeJointOccupancy) and $2,000 times line 29g (/form5695Line32aOwnPaidHeatPumpsBiomass) divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants for the property (that plus /form5695Line32aOthersPaidHeatPumpsBiomassOrZero), rounded to whole dollars, so the share applies whenever the occupants' combined credit exceeds $2,000 (tax interpretation IN-273). With the other occupants' payment unanswered for a property you paid for, this line does not resolve (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033).

Fact.Name: Tentative energy efficient home improvement credit (Form 5695 line 30)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 30 = line 28 + line 29h — the credit before the tax-liability limit (line 31). Resolves whenever lines 28 and 29h do (they do not resolve while a gate question, an other-occupant payment or another named hold is open, IN-277), and the filer has attested to the MFJ two-main-homes special rule (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesApplies, §25C(f)(2)(B)), in which case the second home's own line 30 (/writableMfjSecondMainHomeLine30) is added — unwrapped, so an unanswered second-home figure makes THIS fact Incomplete rather than silently equal to the first home's amount alone. This is the instructions' rule for married taxpayers filing jointly who lived apart in separate main homes: line 30 of both forms combined on one form; the return is not refused (FED-5695-P2-MFJ2HOMES-032). The other home's line 30 is at most its line 28 ($1,200) plus its line 29h ($2,000), $3,200: a figure above that cannot be that form's line 30, so line 30 does not resolve and the return is held with /form5695MfjSecondMainHomeLine30WithinItsCaps as its reason, rather than capped or passed through (tax interpretation IN-275; FED-5695-P2-MFJLINE30CAP-051). TWO-HOMES QUESTION UNANSWERED: when /writableMfjTwoMainHomes is unanswered but the other home's line 30 is entered above $0 on a return that is or may be joint, line 30 does not resolve and the return is held with /form5695MfjTwoMainHomesAnsweredWhenOtherHomeLine30Entered as its reason, never a silent single-home total that drops the other home (tax interpretation IN-277 (d)).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 8 before the joint-occupancy allocation
Fact.Description: Line 8 as figured without the joint-occupancy allocation: the item list's costs taken into account when supplied, otherwise the whole line 8 cost, or its nonbusiness portion when business use is reported (section 25D(e)(7)). Under line 7c this is the occupant's own figure the allocation starts from: section 25D(e)(7) applies first, then (e)(4) (tax interpretation IN-274). GATE UNANSWERED (tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)): with /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse unanswered and a cost above $0, this does not resolve, whether or not a percentage is given, and the return is held (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered): one gate state, one outcome on the typed, printed-box and item-list routes. A $0 or unanswered cost needs no answer.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 8: the whole amount this occupant paid
Fact.Description: The whole fuel cell cost this occupant paid, before any nonbusiness allocation: the item list's whole costs when supplied, otherwise /writableLine8FuelCellCosts, not below $0. It is what the other occupants' payments are measured against.

Fact.Name: Line 7c: what the other occupants paid for the fuel cell property
Fact.Description: /writableFuelCellJointAllOccupantsCosts (all occupants, this one included) less this occupant's whole cost (/form5695Line8FuelCellOwnWholeCost). The allocation's denominator is this occupant's own figure plus this amount (tax interpretation IN-273).

Fact.Name: Line 7c: the joint-occupancy inputs describe one property and are consistent
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 7c applies (/form5695FuelCellJointWorksheetSelected) and the worksheet cannot be figured: the all-occupant payments or the capacity in watts is unanswered; the single-property confirmation is not Yes; all occupants paid $0 or less; or this occupant's whole cost is more than all occupants paid. TRUE otherwise, and on every return where line 7c does not apply (FED-5695-P1-JOINTOCC-037). Not held when line 7a is answered No: the form then skips lines 7b through 11 and line 11 is $0 (f5695 line 43).

Fact.Name: A fuel cell amount is entered on line 8
Fact.Description: True when line 8 has an amount above $0 (the typed cost or the item list's whole costs) or line 7c's worksheet applies. A line 8 of $0 is no fuel cell amount: line 11 is then $0 whatever line 7a says.

Fact.Name: Line 7a is answered whenever a fuel cell amount is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 8 carries a fuel cell amount (/form5695Line8FuelCellAmountEntered) and line 7a (installed on or in connection with the main home) is unanswered: the credit needs the main-home use a Yes establishes, and line 11 does not resolve until it is answered (FED-5695-P1-FUELCELL7A-038). TRUE otherwise.

Fact.Name: The other main home's line 30 is within that form's caps
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when the two-main-homes rule applies and the other home's typed line 30 (/writableMfjSecondMainHomeLine30) is above $3,200, the most that form's line 28 ($1,200) and line 29h ($2,000) can add to (FED-5695-P2-MFJLINE30CAP-051). TRUE otherwise.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 30, the entry on the dotted line to its left
Fact.Description: "More than one main home" when the two-main-homes rule applies (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesApplies), as step 3 of the instructions directs; not resolved, so nothing is entered, otherwise. Step 4 then has both forms attached to the return: the other home's own completed Form 5695 goes with this one (/form5695SecondMainHomeFormAttached) (FED-5695-P2-MFJ2HOMES-032).

Fact.Name: Both Forms 5695 are attached (two main homes on a joint return)
Fact.Description: True when the two-main-homes rule applies: the return carries both Forms 5695, this one and the other main home's own completed form whose line 30 is /writableMfjSecondMainHomeLine30 (step 4 of the instructions). It tells the return assembler to attach the second form; false otherwise (FED-5695-P2-MFJ2HOMES-032).

Fact.Name: Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit Limit Worksheet line 2 (credits ordered before this credit)
Fact.Description: Worksheet line 2: the total of the credits/adjustments taken on the 2025 return that are applied against tax BEFORE the energy efficient home improvement credit — Schedule 3 line 6l, the foreign tax credit (Schedule 3 line 1), the child and dependent care credit (Schedule 3 line 2), the credit for the elderly or disabled (Schedule 3 line 6d), nonrefundable education credits (Schedule 3 line 3), and the retirement savings contributions credit (Schedule 3 line 4). The printed list STOPS at the saver's credit — no CTC term and no Part I (line 5a) term: this credit is ordered BEFORE both (they subtract Form 5695 line 32 in their own limit worksheets: ctcOdc /sched8812CreditLimit and this module's Part I /form5695CreditLimitWorksheetLine2). Non-circular: none of the six terms depends on /sched3Line5b (grep-verified).

Fact.Name: Limitation based on tax liability (Form 5695 line 31)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 31, from the Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit Limit Worksheet: line 1 (Form 1040 line 18, taxCalculations /totalTentativeTax) minus line 2 (the credits ordered before this credit), floored at 0 ("If zero or less, enter -0- on Form 5695, lines 31 and 32").

Fact.Name: Energy efficient home improvement credit (Form 5695 line 32 → Schedule 3 line 5b)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 32 = smaller of line 30 (/form5695TotalHomeImprovementCredit) and line 31 (/form5695EehicTaxLiabilityLimit). Nonrefundable, NO carryforward (unlike Part I). Flows to Schedule 3 line 5b → /line8OfSchedule3 → Form 1040 line 20; also subtracted inside ctcOdc /sched8812CreditLimit (CLW-A) and this module's Part I limit worksheet — filling the 5b placeholder makes those stacked-credit orderings live. TWO MAIN HOMES: on a joint return where the two-main-homes rule applies (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesApplies), line 30 carries the other home's line 30 even when this home has no Part II cost, so line 32 reads line 30 then too (i5695 steps 1-3; tax interpretation IN-277 (g)); while the two-homes question is unanswered with the other home's line 30 entered on a return that may be joint, line 32 follows line 30 and does not resolve (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesAnsweredWhenOtherHomeLine30Entered, IN-277 (d)). Complete-safe: with no Part II cost line answered and neither two-homes state, the else branch yields 0 WITHOUT evaluating the line 31 limit chain, so every prior scenario keeps /sched3Line5b, /line8OfSchedule3, and /sched8812CreditLimit byte-identical. BASIS: the increase in the basis of the home that the expenditures would otherwise produce is reduced by the amount of this credit allowed. That reduction changes no amount on this year's return; it matters when the home is later sold, so the filer keeps a record of the credit with the home's basis records.

Fact.Name: Line 10 amount as line 11 reads it (Form 5695 line 10)
Fact.Description: Line 10 as line 11 reads it. $0 when line 8 carries no fuel cell amount; with a fuel cell amount and no capacity it does not resolve and the return is held (IN-277). When /form5695FuelCellJointWorksheetSelected is true, use its verified same-property capacity ceiling; a typed line 10 amount (/writableLine10KilowattCapacityLimit), when supplied, must agree with it. The shared cost allocation is performed on line 8, once. Off the joint worksheet, line 10 comes from the two printed capacity boxes (/form5695Line10CapacityFromPrintedKilowatts) when either is answered; otherwise from the typed line 10 amount taken down to whole half kilowatts (/form5695Line10TypedLimitInWholeHalfKilowatts); otherwise $0 only when line 8 carries no fuel cell amount. Capacity counts only in whole half kilowatts, $500 each (FED-5695-P1-FUELCELLKW-039). Off the worksheet (for example on a joint return with line 7c checked), an answered capacity in watts decides line 10 ahead of a typed amount (tax interpretation IN-275). With a fuel cell amount on line 8 and no capacity given it does not resolve, and the return is held (/form5695Line10CapacityAnsweredWhenFuelCellAmountEntered; IN-277); $0 only when line 8 carries no fuel cell amount.

Fact.Name: Fuel cell credit allowed after the kilowatt capacity limit (Form 5695 line 11)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 11, the smaller of line 9 and line 10, when line 7a is answered Yes (the fuel cell property is on or in connection with the main home in the United States). $0 when line 7a is answered No, because the form skips lines 7b through 11 (/form5695Line7aAnsweredNo). With line 7a unanswered: $0 when line 8 carries no fuel cell amount (/form5695Line8FuelCellAmountEntered false, including a line 8 of $0); otherwise line 11 does not resolve and the return is held with /form5695Line7aAnsweredWhenFuelCellAmountEntered as its reason, because the credit needs the main-home use a Yes establishes (FED-5695-P1-FUELCELL7A-038). One of the three addends /form5695Line13TotalCredit reads.

Fact.Name: Line 12 carryforward as line 13 reads it, zero when unanswered (Form 5695 line 12)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine12CarryforwardFrom2024: the entered amount when line 12 is answered, else 0, so line 13 resolves for a filer with no carryforward.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 12 as printed: the 2024 carryforward, not below zero
Fact.Description: The amount printed on Form 5695 line 12: the filer's /writableLine12CarryforwardFrom2024, not below $0. Line 12 is the amount from the 2024 Form 5695 line 16, a carryforward of unused credit, which is never negative, and line 13 already adds the floored amount (/form5695Line12CarryforwardOrZero), so a negative answer prints $0 and the printed line 13 foots. It does not resolve, and so prints blank, when line 12 is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Total residential clean energy credit before the tax liability limit (Form 5695 line 13)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 13, "Add lines 6b, 11, and 12": /form5695TentativeCredit for line 6b, /form5695Line11FuelCellCreditAllowed for line 11, /form5695Line12CarryforwardOrZero for line 12. Lines 6b and 12 are complete safe. Line 11 is too on a return with no fuel cell amount, but it does not resolve while a line 8 amount (or a line 8 item list) is entered and line 7a is unanswered, and so neither does this line; and line 6a does not resolve while a per-item list does not add up to its line's whole cost. This is the amount the line 14/15 limit chain applies to — both /residentialCleanEnergyCredit's plain arm and its Worksheet B twin /residentialCleanEnergyCreditWsb read it as their LesserOf numerator.

Fact.Name: Line 14 limit on the plain Credit Limit Worksheet arm, zero otherwise (Form 5695 line 14)
Fact.Description: The plain arm of printed line 14: /form5695TaxLiabilityLimit when the filer is NOT directed to Credit Limit Worksheet B, else 0. The complement of /form5695Line14LimitWorksheetBArm.

Fact.Name: Line 14 limit on the Credit Limit Worksheet B arm, zero otherwise (Form 5695 line 14)
Fact.Description: The Worksheet B arm of printed line 14: /form5695TaxLiabilityLimitWsb when ctcOdc /isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB is true, else 0. One of the two arms whose sum is the printed box; exactly one is ever nonzero because the two conditions are a Bool and its Not.

Fact.Name: Limitation based on tax liability as line 14 prints it (Form 5695 line 14)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 14, the amount from the Residential Clean Energy Credit Limit Worksheet, selected between the two arms the shipping dictionary already computes. It is the sum of the two arm facts because their conditions are a Bool and its Not: exactly one arm carries the limit and the other is 0, so the Add is an exact selector and not an addition of two limits. This is the box the SEVERAL-FACTS lead saw two candidate facts for; neither of them is the printed value on its own.

Fact.Name: Residential clean energy credit carryforward to 2026 (Form 5695 line 16)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 16, line 13 minus line 15. Line 15 is the smaller of lines 13 and 14, so the difference is never negative and the printed condition that line 15 be less than line 13 needs no separate test: when they are equal the result is 0, which is what the box shows. Subtrahend is the shipping /residentialCleanEnergyCredit, the line 15 selector. Print only: nothing consumes this fact, and a 2026 return is not filed from it (the 2026 return carries it on its own line 12).

Fact.Name: Line 17a No box: the qualified energy efficiency improvements are not installed in or on a main home located in the United States (Form 5695 line 17a)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 5695 line 17a, the negation of the shipping Yes box /writableEeImprovementsInMainHome that the register already prints. Incomplete while the question is unanswered, so neither box prints until the filer answers. A No on any of lines 17a, 17b or 17c bars the energy efficient home improvement credit, and the shipping /form5695SectionAQualified already enforces that from the Yes boxes; this fact only prints.

Fact.Name: Line 17b No box: the filer is not the original user of the qualified energy efficiency improvements (Form 5695 line 17b)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 5695 line 17b, the negation of the shipping Yes box /writableEeImprovementsOriginalUser that the register already prints. Incomplete while the question is unanswered, so neither box prints until the filer answers. A No on any of lines 17a, 17b or 17c bars the energy efficient home improvement credit, and the shipping /form5695SectionAQualified already enforces that from the Yes boxes; this fact only prints.

Fact.Name: Line 17c No box: the components are not reasonably expected to remain in use for at least 5 years (Form 5695 line 17c)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 5695 line 17c, the negation of the shipping Yes box /writableEeImprovementsExpected5Years that the register already prints. Incomplete while the question is unanswered, so neither box prints until the filer answers. A No on any of lines 17a, 17b or 17c bars the energy efficient home improvement credit, and the shipping /form5695SectionAQualified already enforces that from the Yes boxes; this fact only prints.

Fact.Name: Line 17e No box: none of the improvements were related to the construction of the main home (Form 5695 line 17e)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 5695 line 17e, the negation of the shipping Yes box /writableEeImprovementsConstructionRelated that the register already prints. Incomplete while line 17e is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Cost of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 19d, the total of the two itemized door costs on lines 19d(i) and 19d(ii), each $0 without its own printed QMID. /form5695Line19fOtherDoorCosts (line 19f) adds it to the line 19e statement. A typed line 19f total /writableOtherDoorCosts adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271).

Fact.Name: Line 19d(i) door cost as the line 19d total reads it, zero when unanswered (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine19dEntry1Cost: the entered cost of the first of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors when it is answered AND its own QMID (/writableLine19dEntry1QmidFirst4) is also answered, else 0. §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item"); a door itemized here without its own QMID contributes 0 to the line 19d total even though the line 19b QMID of the line 19a door is answered. Same shape as /form5695Line20aEntry1CostOrZero on the window line, so the line 19d total foots with one, two or no entries.

Fact.Name: Line 19d(ii) door cost as the line 19d total reads it, zero when unanswered (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine19dEntry2Cost: the entered cost of the second of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors when it is answered AND its own QMID (/writableLine19dEntry2QmidFirst4) is also answered, else 0. §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item"); a door itemized here without its own QMID contributes 0 to the line 19d total even though the line 19b QMID of the line 19a door is answered. Same shape as /form5695Line20aEntry1CostOrZero on the window line, so the line 19d total foots with one, two or no entries.

Fact.Name: Line 20a(i) window or skylight cost, 0 when unanswered (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine20aEntry1Cost: a taxpayer who bought fewer than four windows leaves the remaining itemization rows blank, and the line 20a total must still resolve. Requires its own QMID (/writableLine20aEntry1QmidFirst4) to be answered too — §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item") — else this entry contributes 0. Unanswered means 0.

Fact.Name: Line 20a(ii) window or skylight cost, 0 when unanswered (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine20aEntry2Cost: a taxpayer who bought fewer than four windows leaves the remaining itemization rows blank, and the line 20a total must still resolve. Requires its own QMID (/writableLine20aEntry2QmidFirst4) to be answered too — §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item") — else this entry contributes 0. Unanswered means 0.

Fact.Name: Line 20a(iii) window or skylight cost, 0 when unanswered (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine20aEntry3Cost: a taxpayer who bought fewer than four windows leaves the remaining itemization rows blank, and the line 20a total must still resolve. Requires its own QMID (/writableLine20aEntry3QmidFirst4) to be answered too — §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item") — else this entry contributes 0. Fact.Name: Line 20a(iv) window or skylight cost, 0 when unanswered (Form 5695 line 20a)

Requires its own QMID (/writableLine20aEntry4QmidFirst4) to be answered too — §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item") — else this entry contributes 0. Unanswered means 0.

Fact.Name: Cost of the four most expensive exterior windows and skylights (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 20a, the sum of the four itemized window and skylight costs on lines 20a(i) through 20a(iv), each $0 without its own printed QMID. /form5695Line20cWindowSkylightCosts (line 20c) adds it to the line 20b statement. A typed category total /writableWindowSkylightCosts adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 21a answered No
Fact.Description: The line 21a No box: true when /writableEnergyPropertyInUsHome is false. Unanswered stays incomplete so neither the Yes box nor the No box prints.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 21b answered No
Fact.Description: The line 21b No box: true when /writableEnergyPropertyOriginalUse is false. Unanswered stays incomplete so neither box prints.

Fact.Name: Line 23a(i) water heater cost, 0 when unanswered (Form 5695 line 23a)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine23aEntry1Cost so the printed line 23a subtotal resolves when the filer reports fewer than two water heaters. Requires its own QMID (/writableLine23aEntry1QmidFirst4) to be answered too — §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item") — else this entry contributes 0. Unanswered means 0.

Fact.Name: Line 23a(ii) water heater cost, 0 when unanswered (Form 5695 line 23a)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine23aEntry2Cost so the printed line 23a subtotal resolves when the filer reports fewer than two water heaters. Requires its own QMID (/writableLine23aEntry2QmidFirst4) to be answered too — §25C(h)(1) disallows per item ("any item of specified property ... such item") — else this entry contributes 0. Unanswered means 0.

Fact.Name: Cost of the two most expensive natural gas, propane, or oil water heaters (Form 5695 line 23a)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 23a as printed, the sum of the two entry costs on lines 23a(i) and 23a(ii), each $0 without its own printed QMID. /form5695Line23cFossilFuelWaterHeaterCosts (line 23c) adds it to the line 23b statement. A typed category total /writableFossilFuelWaterHeaterCosts adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 25a answered No
Fact.Description: True when the filer answered No to Form 5695 line 25a, the enabling property question, so the printed No box is checked and lines 25b through 25e are skipped. Not of the existing answer /writableEnablingPropertyInstalled2025, which the configuration already maps to the Yes box. Unanswered stays incomplete, so neither box is checked. Same shape as /form5695Line21aNo from the offset 39 work item.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 26a answered No
Fact.Description: True when the filer answered No to Form 5695 line 26a, the home energy audit question, so the printed No box is checked and the audit credit is not claimed. Not of the existing answer /writableHomeEnergyAuditQualified, which the configuration already maps to the Yes box. Unanswered stays incomplete, so neither box is checked.

Fact.Name: Line 5a No box: battery storage capacity is not at least 3 kilowatt hours (Form 5695 line 5a)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 5695 line 5a. It is the negation of the shipping Yes box /writableBatteryStorageAtLeast3kwh, which the register already prints in c1_1[0]. Incomplete while line 5a is unanswered, so an unanswered question prints neither box, which is what the printed pair means.

Fact.Name: Line 7a No box: qualified fuel cell property was not installed on the main home (Form 5695 line 7a)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 5695 line 7a, the negation of /writableLine7aFuelCellInMainHome. Incomplete while line 7a is unanswered, so neither box prints until the filer answers.

Fact.Name: Line 8 fuel cell costs as line 9 reads them, zero when unanswered (Form 5695 line 8)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine8FuelCellCosts: the entered amount when line 8 is answered, else 0. It is what keeps line 9, and therefore lines 11, 13 and 16, resolving on a return with no fuel cell entry, exactly as /form5695QualifiedCleanEnergyCosts does for lines 1 through 5b. When /form5695FuelCellJointWorksheetSelected is true, use the reconciled joint-occupancy cost from /form5695FuelCellJointAllocatedCost. Missing or unsupported selected sources stay Incomplete. The previous nonshared cost/nonbusiness-use behavior remains when the line 7c checkbox is not selected. A supplied line 8 item list counts as answered (FED-5695-NONBUSINESS80-013).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 7a is answered No
Fact.Description: TRUE only when /writableLine7aFuelCellInMainHome is answered No: the filer may not claim a credit for qualified fuel cell property, and lines 7b through 11 are skipped. An unanswered line 7a reads as not No, so this fact is always complete and no filer who never sees the fuel cell question is held up by it.

Fact.Name: Tentative fuel cell credit, 30 percent of line 8 (Form 5695 line 9)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 9, line 8 multiplied by 30 percent (0.30), rounded, computed as Round(line 8 x 30 / 100). Identical arithmetic to the shipping line 6b fact. $0 when line 7a is answered No: the form says a No means no credit for qualified fuel cell property and skips lines 7b through 11, so a line 8 amount entered anyway earns nothing. An UNANSWERED line 7a does not gate the line: a Switch that waited on it would make this line, and lines 11, 13 and 16 with it, Incomplete for every filer who never sees the fuel cell question.

Fact.Name: This filer is not directed to Credit Limit Worksheet B (Form 5695 line 14)
Fact.Description: The negation of ctcOdc /isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB, the Schedule 8812 Credit Limit Worksheet A line 3 trigger. It exists so the printed line 14 can select the plain arm with the same Switch shape the Worksheet B arm uses.

Fact.Name: Denominator of the 30 percent residential clean energy rate (Form 5695 lines 6b and 9)
Fact.Description: The 100 of the 30 percent applicable percentage. See /form5695ThirtyPercentNumerator; the pair expresses the printed rate as a part over a whole for the ratable template.

Fact.Name: Numerator of the 30 percent residential clean energy rate (Form 5695 lines 6b and 9)
Fact.Description: The 30 in the 30 percent applicable percentage the printed form applies on lines 6b and 9. It exists because the ratable template expresses a rate as a part over a whole; paired with /form5695ThirtyPercentDenominator it renders Round(costs x 30 / 100), the same value the shipping /form5695TentativeCredit gets from Round(3/10 x costs).

Fact.Name: Part I home address, city or town (Form 5695 Part I address block)
Fact.Description: The city or town of the home where the filer installed the property or technology reported on Form 5695 Part I lines 1 through 4 and 5b. The printed block sits above line 1 and carries no line number of its own. It is reporting detail: no Part I computation reads it. String because the box is free text and the shipping graph has no fact for the property home, which need not be the filer mailing address on Form 1040 and need not be a main home.

Fact.Name: Part I home address, state (Form 5695 Part I address block)
Fact.Description: The state of the home where the filer installed the property or technology reported on Form 5695 Part I lines 1 through 4 and 5b. The printed block sits above line 1 and carries no line number of its own. It is reporting detail: no Part I computation reads it. String because the box is free text and the shipping graph has no fact for the property home, which need not be the filer mailing address on Form 1040 and need not be a main home.

Fact.Name: Part I home address, street address (Form 5695 Part I address block)
Fact.Description: The street address of the home where the filer installed the property or technology reported on Form 5695 Part I lines 1 through 4 and 5b. The printed block sits above line 1 and carries no line number of its own. It is reporting detail: no Part I computation reads it. String because the box is free text and the shipping graph has no fact for the property home, which need not be the filer mailing address on Form 1040 and need not be a main home.

Fact.Description: The unit number of the home where the filer installed the property or technology reported on Form 5695 Part I lines 1 through 4 and 5b. The printed block sits above line 1 and carries no line number of its own. It is reporting detail: no Part I computation reads it.
