Fact.Name: Part I home address, ZIP code (Form 5695 Part I address block)
Fact.Description: The ZIP code of the home where the filer installed the property or technology reported on Form 5695 Part I lines 1 through 4 and 5b. The printed block sits above line 1 and carries no line number of its own. It is reporting detail: no Part I computation reads it. String because the box is free text and the shipping graph has no fact for the property home, which need not be the filer mailing address on Form 1040 and need not be a main home.

Fact.Name: Line 10 kilowatt capacity, the digits after the decimal point (Form 5695 line 10)
Fact.Description: The fractional digits of the capacity of the qualified fuel cell property reported on line 8, the second of the two printed capacity boxes (for 1.3 kW enter 3; for 2.05 kW enter 05). String, not Int, because the box is a digit field where a leading zero is significant: 05 and 5 are different capacities and an Int would collapse them. Capacity counts only in half kW increments, so this box adds $500 to line 10 exactly when its first digit is 5 through 9 (/form5695Line10CapacityFromPrintedKilowatts).

Fact.Name: Line 10 amount: kilowatt capacity multiplied by $1,000 (Form 5695 line 10)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 10 as a typed amount: the capacity of the fuel cell property multiplied by $1,000. Read only when neither printed capacity box (/writableLine10KilowattCapacityWholeNumber, /writableLine10KilowattCapacityDecimals) is answered, and then taken down to whole half kilowatts (/form5695Line10TypedLimitInWholeHalfKilowatts), because the credit is $500 for each half kilowatt and capacity is claimed only in half kW increments. On the joint worksheet a supplied amount must agree with the computed ceiling.

Fact.Name: Line 10 kilowatt capacity, the digits before the decimal point (Form 5695 line 10)
Fact.Description: The whole kilowatts of capacity of the qualified fuel cell property reported on line 8, the first of the two printed capacity boxes. Line 10 is figured from this box and the decimal box beside it (/form5695Line10CapacityFromPrintedKilowatts): $1,000 for each whole kilowatt, in whole half kilowatts. Enter 0 for a capacity under 1 kW. Validation: Int, Min 0. A capacity cannot be negative: the reader floors a negative answer at 0 (/form5695Line10CapacityFromPrintedKilowatts), and the return is held as an invalid answer (/form5695NumericAnswersNotNegative; tax interpretation IN-277 (f)), never a silent $0 on line 10 and line 11.

Fact.Name: Residential clean energy credit carryforward from 2024 (Form 5695 line 12)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 12, the unused residential clean energy credit carried into 2025 from the filer 2024 Form 5695 line 16. A prior year figure the graph cannot compute; collected as a filer entry, complete-safe 0 when unanswered (/form5695Line12CarryforwardOrZero), and read into /form5695Line13TotalCredit and (via /residentialCleanEnergyPartIIsActive) the Part I input gate.

Fact.Name: Line 17d main home address, city or town (Form 5695 line 17d)
Fact.Description: The city or town of the main home where the filer made the qualifying energy efficiency improvements, Form 5695 line 17d. Reporting detail: no Part II computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 17d main home address, state (Form 5695 line 17d)
Fact.Description: The state of the main home where the filer made the qualifying energy efficiency improvements, Form 5695 line 17d. Reporting detail: no Part II computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 17d main home address, street address (Form 5695 line 17d)
Fact.Description: The street address of the main home where the filer made the qualifying energy efficiency improvements, Form 5695 line 17d. Reporting detail: no Part II computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 17d main home address, unit number (Form 5695 line 17d)
Fact.Description: The unit number of the main home where the filer made the qualifying energy efficiency improvements, Form 5695 line 17d. Reporting detail: no Part II computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 17d main home address, ZIP code (Form 5695 line 17d)
Fact.Description: The ZIP code of the main home where the filer made the qualifying energy efficiency improvements, Form 5695 line 17d. Reporting detail: no Part II computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs. Its MFJ exception (a return where each spouse has a different main home) is /writableMfjTwoMainHomes below.

Fact.Name: Married filing jointly, spouses lived apart in separate main homes (Form 5695 Part II special rule)
Fact.Description: Screen question: "During 2025, did you and your spouse live apart, each of you owning and using a different home as your main home, and are you both claiming the energy efficient home improvement credit for improvements made to your separate main homes?" Help text: i5695's "Married taxpayers with more than one home" rule (page 3): the credit limits apply to each spouse's main home separately (section 25C(f)(2)(B)), and on a joint return the instructions have the filer complete lines 17a through 30 of a separate Form 5695 for each main home and enter the combined line 30 on one of the forms. Asked-when: filing status MFJ and the filer has answered a Part II gate (line 17a or line 21a). When the rule applies, line 30 carries the other home's line 30 even with no Part II cost on this home, and line 32 and /form5695IsRequired read it (IN-277 (g)). Unanswered posture: with no other-home line 30 entered, not reported: a filer never asked has not reported separate main homes, and the single-home Part II computation applies unchanged. Unanswered with the other home's line 30 (/writableMfjSecondMainHomeLine30) entered above $0 on a return that is or may be joint: the return is held (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesAnsweredWhenOtherHomeLine30Entered) and line 30 does not resolve, never a silent drop of that home (tax interpretation IN-277 (d)). Validation: Boolean, required only when the asked-when gate is met. Feeds /form5695MfjTwoMainHomesApplies, which requires /writableMfjSecondMainHomeLine30 (the other home's own line 30, figured on its own copy) before /form5695TotalHomeImprovementCredit resolves; line 30 then adds it. A Yes does not refuse the return (FED-5695-P2-MFJ2HOMES-032).

Fact.Name: The MFJ two-main-homes special rule is in force on this return (Form 5695 Part II)
Fact.Description: True when /writableMfjTwoMainHomes is answered Yes on a joint return (filing status married filing jointly). The combined line 30 is figured only on a joint return (i5695 line 188), so a Yes left over on any other return adds nothing (FED-5695-P2-MFJ2HOMES-032). FALSE when unanswered or not a joint return; an unanswered question with the other home's line 30 entered is held separately (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesAnsweredWhenOtherHomeLine30Entered, IN-277 (d)). Read by /form5695TotalHomeImprovementCredit (line 30), /energyEfficientHomeImprovementCredit (line 32) and /form5695IsRequired, so a joint return whose second home alone carries the cost still reaches line 32 (IN-277 (g)). With Yes answered and the filing status not yet known it does not resolve, so line 30 waits rather than assuming either way.

Fact.Name: Second main home's own line 30 amount (Form 5695 Part II, MFJ two-main-homes special rule)
Fact.Description: Screen question, asked only when /writableMfjTwoMainHomes is Yes: "Figure the energy efficient home improvement credit for your spouse's separate main home the same way you figured it above (Form 5695, Part II, lines 17a through 30), using a separate copy of the form for that home. Enter the amount from line 30 of that separate form here." Help text: i5695's "Married taxpayers with more than one home" steps 1-2: "Complete lines 17a through 30 of a separate Form 5695 for each main home. Figure the amount to be entered on line 30 of both forms and enter the combined amount on line 30 of one of the forms." This dictionary computes this home's line 30 (/form5695CombinedCappedCredit + /form5695HeatPumpBiomassCredit) and adds the other home's line 30, which the filer figures on that home's own copy, where that home's $1,200 and $2,000 caps apply, exactly as the instructions direct. Unanswered posture: while the two-main-homes rule applies, this left unanswered leaves line 30, and therefore Schedule 3 line 5b, unresolved and holds the return (/form5695MfjSecondMainHomeLine30Answered), never a silent single-home total. Feeds /form5695TotalHomeImprovementCredit's guarded arm. The return is not refused when this rule applies (FED-5695-P2-MFJ2HOMES-032). Validation: Dollar, $0 to $3,200 (the other form's line 28 at most $1,200 plus its line 29h at most $2,000); a figure above $3,200 holds the return (IN-275).

Fact.Name: Line 19b Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number, last 13 characters (Form 5695 line 19b)
Fact.Description: The last 13 characters of the QMID reported on Form 5695 line 19b for the most expensive qualifying exterior door. The printed line splits the identifier across a four character box and a thirteen character box; the four character box, /writableMostExpensiveDoorQmid, is the QMID that decides whether the line 19a door counts (tax interpretation IN-271). This box is printed detail and gates nothing. Validation: at most 13 characters, the printed box's length; the source fixes no character set for these characters, so none is enforced.

Fact.Name: Line 19d(i) cost of the second most expensive qualifying exterior door (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: Cost of the first door itemized on Form 5695 line 19d(i), one of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors. Read through /form5695Line19dEntry1CostOrZero; the derived category total uses the component lines whenever any of them is answered, else the filer typed category total. Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the item's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableLine19dEntry1NonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1) importing §25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695Line19dEntry1CostTakenIntoAccount). LABOR: do not include amounts paid for the onsite preparation, assembly, or original installation of the component. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. SUBSIDIES AND FINANCING: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf, and exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing (financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or energy-production projects). STANDARD: the door must meet the applicable Energy Star requirements.

Fact.Name: Line 19d(i) Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number, first four characters (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: The first four characters of the QMID reported for the first of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors on Form 5695 line 19d(i). Companion of the staged /writableLine19dEntry1QmidLast13, which stays reporting detail. This box, together with /writableLine19dEntry1Cost, gates whether THIS door's cost reaches the line 19d total — §25C(h)(1) requires a QMID per item, so an itemized door without its own QMID here contributes 0 even when the line 19b QMID of the line 19a door (/writableMostExpensiveDoorQmid) is answered.

Fact.Name: Line 19d(i) Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number, last 13 characters (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: The last 13 characters of the QMID reported for the first of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors on Form 5695 line 19d(i). The printed form splits this QMID across a four character box and a thirteen character box; this fact is the second box only. The first box, /writableLine19dEntry1QmidFirst4, is the QMID that decides whether the entry counts (tax interpretation IN-271); this box is printed detail and gates nothing. Validation: at most 13 characters, the printed box's length; the source fixes no character set for these characters, so none is enforced.

Fact.Name: Line 19d(ii) cost of the third most expensive qualifying exterior door (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: Cost of the second door itemized on Form 5695 line 19d(ii). Read through /form5695Line19dEntry2CostOrZero; the derived category total uses the component lines whenever any of them is answered, else the filer typed category total. Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the item's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableLine19dEntry2NonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1) importing §25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695Line19dEntry2CostTakenIntoAccount). LABOR: do not include amounts paid for the onsite preparation, assembly, or original installation of the component. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. SUBSIDIES AND FINANCING: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf, and exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing (financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or energy-production projects). STANDARD: the door must meet the applicable Energy Star requirements.

Fact.Name: Line 19d(ii) Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number, first four characters (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: The first four characters of the QMID reported for the second of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors on Form 5695 line 19d(ii). This box, together with /writableLine19dEntry2Cost, gates whether THIS door's cost reaches the line 19d total — §25C(h)(1) requires a QMID per item, so an itemized door without its own QMID here contributes 0 even when the line 19b QMID of the line 19a door (/writableMostExpensiveDoorQmid) is answered.

Fact.Name: Line 19d(ii) Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number, last 13 characters (Form 5695 line 19d)
Fact.Description: The last 13 characters of the QMID reported for the second of the two next most expensive qualifying exterior doors on Form 5695 line 19d(ii). The first box, /writableLine19dEntry2QmidFirst4, is the QMID that decides whether the entry counts (tax interpretation IN-271); this box is printed detail and gates nothing. Validation: at most 13 characters, the printed box's length; the source fixes no character set for these characters, so none is enforced.

Fact.Name: Cost of all other qualifying exterior doors (Form 5695 line 19e)
Fact.Description: Amounts paid in 2025 for every qualifying exterior door other than the most expensive door (line 19a) and the two itemized on line 19d. The QMID and cost of each such door go on an attached statement. Enter the whole cost. Its nonbusiness-use percentage is not asked for this typed amount, which adds $0; each statement item carries its own share. For exact mixed-item use and separate QMIDs, supply /form5695Line19eOtherDoorItems. With that collection, this scalar is optional and is a reconciliation of the WHOLE costs only. LABOR: do not include amounts paid for the onsite preparation, assembly, or original installation of the component. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. EARNS NO CREDIT: an amount entered here names no item's QMID, and section 25C(h)(1) allows the credit only for an item whose own QMID is on the return, so it adds $0 to the credit. Itemize each item with its QMID on the printed line or the attached statement instead.

Fact.Name: Line 20a(i) cost of the first most expensive exterior window or skylight (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: Amount paid for the first of the four most expensive exterior windows or skylights that meet the Energy Star certification requirements, itemized on Form 5695 line 20a(i). Summed into /form5695Line20aWindowCost. Enter the whole cost. With 2, line 25d(ii) is required; with 3 or more the items cannot all be reported on the form and the return is held (/form5695EnablingPropertyQmidsReported) (FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048). Validation: Int, at least 1.

Fact.Name: Every enabling property item in line 25c has its QMID box on line 25d
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 25c has a cost and the item count says the cost covers two items with line 25d(ii) blank, or three or more items (the form prints two QMID boxes). It reads nothing behind a skip: with line 21a or 21b answered No, or line 25a not answered Yes, it is TRUE (the form skips lines 25b through 25e).

Fact.Name: Special rule for joint occupants applies (Form 5695 line 32a)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 32a, the box the filer checks when the special rule for joint occupants applies and a statement is attached explaining how the credit was allocated. Answer Yes only if this applies: a home occupied jointly with someone other than a spouse on a joint return, where the qualifying costs were paid by more than one occupant. With Yes, each Part II credit line is the smaller of its usual figure and the property's credit limit times the amount you paid divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (the /writableLine32aOthersPaid* answers), line 28 is limited the same way against $1,200 when line 27 is over $1,200, and line 29h against $2,000 (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCC-033). Read through /form5695Line32aJointOccupantsRuleApplies.

Fact.Name: The joint-occupants special rule is in force on this return (Form 5695 line 32a)
Fact.Description: /writableLine32aJointOccupantsRule when the box is ANSWERED, else FALSE: the complete-safe IsComplete/Switch guard idiom. The Part II credit lines read it to decide whether the joint-occupancy allocation applies; FALSE when unanswered keeps every return that never reaches line 32 on the usual computation. TYPE: Boolean; no sign or rounding.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 Section A is closed: line 17a, 17b or 17c answered No
Fact.Description: True when Section A is closed by an answer: line 17a, 17b or 17c answered No (the form says the filer cannot claim the credit for Section A), or line 17e answered Yes (improvements related to the construction of the home skip lines 18a through 20d, i5695 line 363). Each printed Section A cost line and each Section A credit is then $0 (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050; tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 Section B is closed: line 21a or 21b answered No
Fact.Description: True when line 21a or 21b is answered No. The form then says to skip lines 22 through 25 and line 29, so each of those printed cost lines is $0 (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 Section A: no cost waits on an unanswered line 17 question
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when a Section A cost that could earn credit is entered (line 18a, 19a, 19d, 20a, or a line 19e or 20b statement) while Section A is neither closed by an answer (/form5695SectionAAnsweredNo) nor open (/form5695SectionAQualified: 17a, 17b and 17c Yes and 17e No; an unanswered 17e holds like an unanswered 17a, tax interpretation IN-278). While it is FALSE the printed Section A cost lines and credits do not resolve; TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 Section B: no cost waits on an unanswered line 21 question
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when a Section B cost that could earn credit is entered (line 22a, 23a, 24a, 25c, 29a, 29c, 29e, or a line 22b, 23b, 24b, 29b, 29d or 29f statement) while line 21a or 21b is unanswered and neither is No. While it is FALSE the printed Section B cost lines and credits do not resolve; TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 26a is answered whenever a home energy audit cost is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 26b has a cost above $0 and line 26a is unanswered; line 26b and line 26c then do not resolve. TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 5a is answered whenever a battery storage cost is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when a line 5b battery storage cost above $0 (or a line 5b item list) is entered and line 5a (capacity of at least 3 kilowatt hours) is unanswered; line 6a then does not resolve. TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 25a is answered No
Fact.Description: True when line 25a is answered No: the form says the filer cannot claim the credit for enabling property and skips lines 25b through 25e, so line 25c and line 25e are $0 in every reader (line 28's numerator, the print, the allocation flag, the item-count hold) (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050; tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 25a is answered whenever an enabling property cost is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 25c has a cost above $0, Section B is not closed by an answer, and line 25a is unanswered; line 25c and line 25e then do not resolve. TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 10 has a capacity whenever line 8 carries a fuel cell amount
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 8 carries a fuel cell amount, line 7a is not answered No, and no capacity is given (no printed kilowatt box, no typed line 10 amount and no capacity in watts); line 10 and line 11 then do not resolve rather than giving $0. TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: No Form 5695 amount, capacity or percentage is answered below zero
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when any Form 5695 amount, count, capacity or percentage answer (each cost line the computation reads, each line 19d, 20a and 23a entry, each nonbusiness-use percentage that can be read, the line 10 kilowatt box and typed amount, the line 12 carryforward, the joint-occupancy amounts and watts, the other occupants' payments, the other main home's line 30 and the line 25d item count) is answered below zero. None of these can be negative on the form, so a negative answer is not what the form asks: the return is held as an invalid answer rather than resolving that line to a silent $0 (each reader still floors at $0, so no line goes negative). An item on a Part I item list or a line b statement with a cost below zero leaves its list unresolved and holds the return through /form5695ItemListsResolve. The sixteen typed category totals and typed line b amounts that add $0, and their sixteen percentages that are not asked and not read (tax interpretation IN-271), are not checked here: nothing reads them, so nothing holds on them. TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277 (f)).

Fact.Name: The Form 5695 80 percent nonbusiness-use question is answered whenever a cost is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is unanswered and a cost above $0 sits on an open route: a typed Part I line 1-4, line 5b (not after a No on line 5a) or line 8 (not after a No on line 7a); a Part I item list; line 18a or a printed Section A item line with its QMID box (Section A not closed by an answer); a line 19e or 20b statement; a printed Section B item line with its QMID box, line 25c with its QMID box (not after a No on line 25a), or a Section B statement (Section B not closed by an answer). Section 25D(e)(7) takes into account only the nonbusiness portion of an item used less than 80 percent for nonbusiness purposes, so while the question is unanswered no such cost can be figured: each one does not resolve, on the typed, printed-box and item-list routes alike, even for an item that carries its own share (one gate state, one outcome; tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)). A typed category total or typed line b amount adds $0 (IN-271) and is not read here. TRUE otherwise.

Fact.Name: Every supplied Form 5695 item list or statement resolves
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when a supplied Part I item list or line b statement does not resolve, for example an item with a positive cost and no nonbusiness-use share while the business-use question is Yes or unanswered, a statement with items and no inventory-complete confirmation, a typed line total that contradicts the items, or an item whose cost is answered below zero (an invalid answer, tax interpretation IN-277 (f)). A statement behind a Section closed by an answer is not read, and neither is a line 5b item list after a No on line 5a or a line 8 item list after a No on line 7a: the form says no credit is claimed for that property then, so nothing behind the skip is asked or held (FED-5695-ALLOCCOMPLETE-045; tax interpretation IN-277). TRUE otherwise (FED-5695-ALLOCCOMPLETE-045).

Fact.Name: The other main home's line 30 is answered whenever the two-main-homes rule applies
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when the two-main-homes rule applies (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesApplies) and the other home's own line 30 (/writableMfjSecondMainHomeLine30) is unanswered; line 30 then does not resolve. TRUE otherwise.

Fact.Name: The two-main-homes question is answered whenever the other main home's line 30 is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when the other main home's line 30 (/writableMfjSecondMainHomeLine30) is entered above $0, the two-main-homes question (/writableMfjTwoMainHomes) is unanswered, and the return is a joint return or its filing status is not yet known. Line 30, line 32 and Schedule 3 line 5b then do not resolve, rather than silently dropping the other home's line 30. TRUE otherwise: on a return that is not joint the rule cannot apply (i5695 line 188), so the amount is not read and nothing is held (tax interpretation IN-277 (d)).

Fact.Name: Line 32a: the other occupants' payment is answered for every property you paid for
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 32a is checked and, for a property you paid an amount for, what the other occupants paid (/writableLine32aOthersPaid*) is unanswered; that line does not resolve. TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-273).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 32a is answered whenever an other-occupant payment is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when an amount the other occupants paid (/writableLine32aOthersPaid*) is entered above $0, or a populated other-only household door inventory accompanies positive own qualifying door costs, and line 32a is unanswered: whether the joint-occupancy rule applies is undecided. TRUE otherwise (tax interpretation IN-277).

Fact.Name: Every Part I item list adds up to its line's whole cost
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when a Part I item list (lines 1-5b, 8) is supplied together with a typed whole cost for the line that differs from the items' whole costs added: the two answers contradict each other and the line does not resolve (FED-5695-NONBUSINESS80-013). A list with the typed whole cost unanswered computes from the items (i5695 line 273). TRUE otherwise.

Fact.Name: Joint occupancy: amount the other occupants paid for insulation or air sealing material or system (line 18a)
Fact.Description: Asked when the special rule for joint occupants applies (Form 5695 line 32a checked): the total amount that ALL the OTHER occupants of the jointly occupied home paid for insulation or air sealing material or system (line 18a), not including what you paid (your own amount is on the line itself). Enter 0 when no other occupant paid for this property. The credit allocable to you for this property is never more than the credit limit for the property ($ 1,200) times the amount you paid divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695InsulationCredit). With line 32a checked, an amount on the line and this answer blank, that line does not resolve. Dollar, not below zero.

Fact.Name: Joint occupancy: amount you paid for insulation or air sealing material or system (line 18a)
Fact.Description: The amount you paid for insulation or air sealing material or system (line 18a) as this form takes it into account, $0 when none: the numerator of the joint-occupancy fraction.

Fact.Name: Joint occupancy: amount the other occupants paid for insulation or air sealing material or system (line 18a), as the allocation reads it
Fact.Description: /writableLine32aOthersPaidInsulation not below $0 when you paid an amount for this property on this return; $0 when you paid nothing for it, answered or not, because the allocation counts the others' payments only for the corresponding properties (tax interpretation IN-273); otherwise it does not resolve, because the allocation cannot be figured without the other occupants' payments.

Fact.Name: Joint occupancy: amount the other occupants paid for the most expensive exterior door (line 19a)
Fact.Description: Asked when the special rule for joint occupants applies (Form 5695 line 32a checked): the total amount that ALL the OTHER occupants of the jointly occupied home paid for the most expensive exterior door (line 19a), not including what you paid (your own amount is on the line itself). Enter 0 when no other occupant paid for this property. The credit allocable to you for this property is never more than the credit limit for the property ($ 250) times the amount you paid divided by the total paid by you and all other occupants (/form5695MostExpensiveDoorCredit). With line 32a checked, an amount on the line and this answer blank, that line does not resolve. Dollar, not below zero.

Fact.Name: Joint occupancy: amount you paid for the most expensive exterior door (line 19a)

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 18b before the joint-occupancy allocation
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 18b figured as on any return, before the special rule for joint occupants: Form 5695 line 18b = 30% × line 18a, not more than $1,200. Counts only when Section A is available (lines 17a-17e) and line 18a is answered; else 0 (complete-safe). Whole-dollar HALF_UP rounding on the multiplication. No QMID requirement (insulation is not specified property). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section A cost waits on an unanswered line 17 question (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section A is closed by an answer.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 19c before the joint-occupancy allocation
Fact.Description: Whole-dollar observation of the usual credit for this qualifying physical door before joint allocation. Apply the 30 percent rate and individual 250 dollar cap using the exact eligible-cost helper, then round once. The final all-door calculation retains the separate exact contribution until its own printed-line boundary. Missing required qualification information remains unresolved.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 19h before the joint-occupancy allocation
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 19h for a nonjoint claimant sums the individually capped credit for every qualifying physical exterior door and applies the 500 dollar all-door ceiling. Each door is capped at 250 dollars after its own qualifying-use adjustment, independent of input order or printed slot. Keep exact contributions until one final whole-dollar round, except on the face route (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-360, amending IN-300 at line 19h): when the printed lines 19c and 19g carry exactly the statutory per-door amounts (no other door over its $250 limit), line 19h adds the entered, rounded lines 19c and 19g and applies the $500 limit. Raw line 19g remains its printed 30 percent calculation; the statutory per-item adjustment is explained by the door computation statement when the printed shortcut differs.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 20d before the joint-occupancy allocation
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 20d figured as on any return, before the special rule for joint occupants: Form 5695 line 20d = 30% × line 20c, not more than $600 (combined limit for all exterior windows and skylights). Counts only when Section A is available, the window costs are answered, and each window counts only with its own printed QMID (tax interpretation IN-271); else 0. When /form5695Line20bOtherWindowItems is selected, its independently identified item costs and reconciliation control this credit. No category-header QMID substitutes for a missing item QMID, and a header is not required for an unused printed item. Existing dollar ceilings remain. Without a statement (item list), the line b amount is $0: a typed line b amount or a typed category total names no item's QMID and adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271; owner ruling NE-6). QMID RULE: each item's own QMID is checked on its printed line, where an item without one already counts $0, so this line no longer requires an unprinted category-header QMID (FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046, FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section A cost waits on an unanswered line 17 question (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section A is closed by an answer.

No QMID. ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a line 26b cost waits on an unanswered line 26a (/form5695Line26aAnsweredWhenAuditCostEntered); $0 after a No on 26a.

Fact.Name: Joint occupancy: the line 28 numerator, the amounts you paid on lines 18a through 26b
Fact.Description: The sum of the amounts on lines 18a, 19a, 19f, 20a, 20b, 22a, 22b, 23a, 23b, 24a, 24b, 25c and 26b, as this form takes them into account: the numerator of the line 28 fraction under the special rule for joint occupants.

Fact.Name: Joint occupancy: what the other occupants paid for the line 28 properties
Fact.Description: The total the other occupants paid for the properties on lines 18a through 26b; with the line 28 numerator it makes the denominator, the total paid by you and all other occupants for the corresponding properties.

Fact.Name: Condominium or cooperative fractional share (Form 5695 line 32b)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 32b, the box the filer checks when they live in a condominium or cooperative and hold a fractional share of the qualified energy efficiency improvements or residential energy property expenditures. The share itself is in the cost lines: a member of a condominium management association or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs and includes that share on each cost line (each cost intake says so), so the box records that the costs include such a share and adds no amount of its own (section 25D(e)(5)-(6), applied to Part II by section 25C(f)(1)).

Fact.Name: Line 7a Yes box: qualified fuel cell property installed on the main home in the United States (Form 5695 line 7a)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 7a, whether qualified fuel cell property was installed on, or in connection with, the filer main home located in the United States. A No answer bars any credit for qualified fuel cell property and the printed form says to skip lines 7b through 11. Line 11 reads it: No gives $0; Yes lets lines 9 and 10 decide; unanswered with a fuel cell amount on line 8 holds the return (/form5695Line7aAnsweredWhenFuelCellAmountEntered).

Fact.Name: Line 7b main home address, city or town (Form 5695 line 7b)
Fact.Description: The city or town of the main home where the filer installed the qualified fuel cell property, Form 5695 line 7b. Reporting detail: no computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 7b main home address, state (Form 5695 line 7b)
Fact.Description: The state of the main home where the filer installed the qualified fuel cell property, Form 5695 line 7b. Reporting detail: no computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 7b main home address, street address (Form 5695 line 7b)
Fact.Description: The street address of the main home where the filer installed the qualified fuel cell property, Form 5695 line 7b. Reporting detail: no computation reads it. Fact.Name: Line 7b main home address, unit number (Form 5695 line 7b)
Fact.Description: The unit number of the main home where the filer installed the qualified fuel cell property, Form 5695 line 7b. Reporting detail: no computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 7b main home address, ZIP code (Form 5695 line 7b)
Fact.Description: The ZIP code of the main home where the filer installed the qualified fuel cell property, Form 5695 line 7b. Reporting detail: no computation reads it. The printed caution that a filer can have only one main home at a time is a filer instruction, not a check this fact performs.

Fact.Name: Line 7c: the special rule for joint occupants applies (Form 5695 line 7c)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 7c, the checkbox a filer sets when the special rule for joint occupants applies and a statement is attached. Does the joint-occupant rule apply to this shared fuel-cell installation? A Yes selects the single-property joint-cost worksheet and requires its total costs, capacity and scope confirmation. The rule does not apply to married individuals filing jointly. Missing required sources do not permit unallocated costs to reach the credit. Unanswered posture: a check box, so unanswered with no joint-occupancy worksheet amount entered is the unchecked box and line 8 is figured without the allocation; unanswered while an all-occupants amount (/writableFuelCellJointAllOccupantsCosts) is entered with a line 8 amount on a return not known to be joint holds the return (/form5695Line7cAnsweredWhenJointWorksheetAmountEntered) and line 8 does not resolve (tax interpretation IN-277 (c)).

Fact.Name: Qualified fuel cell property costs (Form 5695 line 8)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 8, the costs of qualified fuel cell property. Feeds line 9 (/form5695Line9FuelCellCredit, 30% of line 8) and, via line 11, /form5695Line13TotalCredit and (via /residentialCleanEnergyPartIIsActive) the Part I input gate. Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the item's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableLine8FuelCellNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695Line8FuelCellCostTakenIntoAccount). WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed; for a reconstructed home, when your original use of it begins; for a newly constructed home, when your original use of it begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. LABOR: include labor costs properly allocable to the onsite preparation, assembly, or original installation of the property and for piping or wiring to interconnect it to the home. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. SUBSIDIES: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf. STANDARD: the fuel cell property must have a nameplate capacity of at least one-half kilowatt of electricity using an electrochemical process and an electricity-only generation efficiency greater than 30%.

Fact.Name: Line 19e other-door cost as the line 19f total reads it, zero when unanswered (Form 5695 line 19e)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine19eOtherDoorCosts, the cost of all qualifying exterior doors other than the most expensive one and the two itemized on line 19d. Unanswered means 0, so the line 19f sum foots for a filer who itemized doors on line 19d and reported no others. Same shape as /form5695Line19dEntry1CostOrZero beside it. When /form5695Line19eOtherDoorItems is explicitly supplied, use its reconciled per-item allocation, not the former lowest-percentage approximation. With no statement supplied, the typed line b amount adds $0 (below), and no line percentage is read. A selected incomplete or contradictory statement remains Incomplete. The all-other total is used once by the existing category calculation. NO CREDIT FOR A TYPED TOTAL: the typed line 19e amount /writableLine19eOtherDoorCosts names no item's QMID; its items count only on the line 19e statement, item by item with each QMID, so it adds $0 here. Section 25C(h)(1) allows the credit for an item of specified property only when that item's QMID is on the return (owner ruling NE-6, 2026-09-27: $0, not a refusal). SECTION A CLOSED: $0 when line 17a, 17b or 17c is answered No (/form5695SectionAAnsweredNo), because the form leaves lines 18a through 20d blank then (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section A cost waits on an unanswered line 17 question (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section A is closed by an answer.

Fact.Name: Any Form 5695 line 19d or 19e other-door cost was answered
Fact.Description: True when the filer answered at least one of the three raw other-door cost intakes: the two line 19d itemized entries and the line 19e all-other entry. This is the "was the source answered" predicate that selects the computed line 19f over the filer typed line 19f total, and it is deliberately taken on the RAW writables rather than on /form5695Line19dDoorCost or /form5695Line19eOtherDoorCostsOrZero, which are complete safe and therefore always Complete.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 19f has an amount, from the components or from the typed total
Fact.Description: The gate /form5695OtherDoorCredit (line 19g) reads in place of the bare IsComplete of /writableOtherDoorCosts it used before. It must not be IsComplete of the derived line 19f total: that total is complete safe, so IsComplete on it is true on every return and the door category would claim its credit for a filer who reported no door cost at all.

Fact.Name: Cost of all other qualifying exterior doors (Form 5695 line 19f)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 19f, "Add lines 19d and 19e", as the credit on line 19g reads it. Computed arm: /form5695Line19dDoorCost (the two itemized entries) plus /form5695Line19eOtherDoorCostsOrZero, taken whenever any of the three raw component intakes was answered. A typed category total adds $0 (below); with no component answered this is $0, so the fact is complete safe. NO CREDIT FOR A TYPED TOTAL: the filer typed category total /writableOtherDoorCosts carries no QMID for the items it adds up, so it adds $0 here. Fact.Name: Cost of the most expensive central air conditioner (Form 5695 line 22a)
Fact.Description: The dollar box on Form 5695 line 22a, which the printed form asks for beside the Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number. Includes allocable onsite preparation, assembly and installation labor, as every Section B cost line does. Summed into /form5695Line22cCentralAcCosts through /form5695Line22aCentralAcCostOrZero. Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the item's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableLine22aCentralAcNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1) importing §25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695Line22aCentralAcCostTakenIntoAccount). WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. SUBSIDIES AND FINANCING: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf, and exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing (financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or energy-production projects). STANDARD: the property must meet or exceed the highest efficiency tier (not including any advanced tier) established by the Consortium for Energy Efficiency that is in effect at the beginning of the calendar year in which it is placed in service.

A typed category total adds $0 (below); with no component answered this is $0, so the fact is complete safe. NO CREDIT FOR A TYPED TOTAL: the filer typed category total /writableHeatPumpWaterHeaterCosts carries no QMID for the items it adds up, so it adds $0 here. Section 25C(h)(1) allows the credit for an item of specified property only when that item's QMID is on the return (owner ruling NE-6, 2026-09-27: $0, not a refusal).

Fact.Name: Cost of the most expensive biomass stove or biomass boiler (Form 5695 line 29e)
Fact.Description: The dollar box on Form 5695 line 29e, which the printed form asks for beside the Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number. Includes allocable onsite preparation, assembly and installation labor, as every Section B cost line does. Summed into /form5695Line29BiomassCosts through /form5695Line29eBiomassCostOrZero. Enter the whole cost. If less than 80% of the item's use is for nonbusiness purposes, the filer gives its nonbusiness-use percentage on /writableLine29eBiomassNonbusinessUsePercent and only that share counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1) importing §25D(e)(7); the allocation is /form5695Line29eBiomassCostTakenIntoAccount). WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. SUBSIDIES AND FINANCING: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf, and exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing (financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or energy-production projects). STANDARD: the biomass stove or boiler must have a thermal efficiency rating of at least 75 percent (measured by the higher heating value of the fuel).

Fact.Name: Line 29e cost as the category total reads it, zero when unanswered (Form 5695 line 29e)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine29eBiomassCost. Unanswered means 0, so the Form 5695 lines 29e and 29f sum foots for a filer who reported only the "all other" line beside it.

Fact.Name: Line 29f other-cost as the category total reads it, zero when unanswered (Form 5695 line 29f)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of /writableLine29fOtherBiomassCosts, the cost of all other qualifying biomass stoves and biomass boilers not itemized on the line above it. Unanswered means 0, so the Form 5695 lines 29e and 29f sum foots for a filer who itemized and reported no others. When /form5695Line29fOtherBiomassItems is explicitly supplied, use its reconciled per-item allocation, not the former lowest-percentage approximation. With no statement supplied, the typed line b amount adds $0 (below), and no line percentage is read. A selected incomplete or contradictory statement remains Incomplete. The all-other total is used once by the existing category calculation. NO CREDIT FOR A TYPED TOTAL: the typed line 29f amount /writableLine29fOtherBiomassCosts names no item's QMID; its items count only on the line 29f statement, item by item with each QMID, so it adds $0 here. Section 25C(h)(1) allows the credit for an item of specified property only when that item's QMID is on the return (owner ruling NE-6, 2026-09-27: $0, not a refusal). SECTION B CLOSED: $0 when line 21a or 21b is answered No (/form5695SectionBAnsweredNo), because the form says to skip lines 22 through 25 and line 29 then (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section B cost waits on an unanswered line 21 question (/form5695SectionBQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section B is closed by an answer.

Fact.Name: Any printed component cost line under Form 5695 lines 29e and 29f was answered
Fact.Description: True when the filer answered at least one of the raw component cost intakes that Form 5695 lines 29e and 29f adds: /writableLine29eBiomassCost, /writableLine29fOtherBiomassCosts. This is the "was the source answered" predicate that selects the computed category total over the filer typed one, and it is taken on the RAW writables and never on their complete safe wrappers, which are always Complete and would select the computed arm for a filer who typed only the total.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 lines 29e and 29f has an amount, from the components or from the typed total
Fact.Description: What /form5695HeatPumpBiomassCosts (line 29g) reads in place of the bare IsComplete of /writableBiomassCosts it used before. It must not be IsComplete of /form5695Line29BiomassCosts: that total is complete safe, so IsComplete on it is true on every return and this category would claim its credit for a filer who reported no cost of this kind at all.

Fact.Name: Costs of biomass stoves and biomass boilers (Form 5695 lines 29e and 29f)

Fact.Name: Nonbusiness-use percentage below which a Form 5695 cost is allocated
Fact.Description: The 80 of "If less than 80 percent of the use of an item is for nonbusiness purposes" (§25D(e)(7), imported for Part II by §25C(f)(1)). Every /form5695*CostTakenIntoAccount fact prorates only when its percentage is strictly below this, so exactly 80 counts the whole cost.

Fact.Name: Any Form 5695 property is used less than 80% for nonbusiness purposes
Fact.Description: Question: "Is any property whose cost you entered on Form 5695 used partly for business, such as for a home office or a rented part of the home, so that less than 80% of its use is for nonbusiness purposes?" Help: for such an item only the part of its cost allocable to nonbusiness use counts toward either credit (i5695 lines 62-65; §25D(e)(7), and §25C(f)(1) for Part II); enter the whole cost on each cost line and, after a Yes, each item's nonbusiness-use percentage. Asked when: any Part I or Part II cost line other than the home energy audit has an amount. The application asks it on every return with a cost, so an unanswered gate is a question skipped, not one never shown. Unanswered: with a cost above $0 on an open route (typed, printed box or item list, Part I or Part II) the return is held with /form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered as its reason and each such cost does not resolve, even an item that carries its own share: one gate state, one outcome (tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)); with no cost entered nothing is held. Validation: Boolean. A Yes makes the nonbusiness-use percentage of every answered cost line required: that line's cost matches no Case and resolves Incomplete until the percentage is given. Feeds every /form5695*CostTakenIntoAccount fact and /form5695NonbusinessUseAllocationIsComplete, the flow:/flowIncomplete member that reports the return unfinished while any such percentage is still missing.

Fact.Name: Every entered Form 5695 cost that needs a nonbusiness-use percentage has one (flow:/flowIncomplete member)
Fact.Description: TRUE unless the filer answered /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse Yes and a cost that is taken into account still has no nonbusiness-use share. The question itself left unanswered with a cost behind it is a separate hold, /form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered (tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)). Section 25D(e)(7), applied to Part II by section 25C(f)(1), owes an allocation only for an expenditure taken into account, so the flag reads only those costs: the Part I lines 1-5b and 8 (their line percentage, or when an item list is supplied the items' shares through its allocated cost; line 5b, typed or itemized, not after a No on line 5a, and line 8, typed or itemized, not after a No on line 7a, because the form says no credit is claimed for that property then); line 18a, and each printed item line (19a, 19d(i)-(ii), 20a(i)-(iv), 22a, 23a(i)-(ii), 24a, 25c, 29a, 29c, 29e) once its own printed QMID box is answered; and each line b statement (19e, 20b, 22b, 23b, 24b, 29b, 29d, 29f) through its applied cost. A Part II cost owes nothing once its section is closed by an answer (/form5695SectionAAnsweredNo, /form5695SectionBAnsweredNo). It reads no typed category total, no typed line b amount and none of their percentages: those add $0 (tax interpretation IN-271). It is a member of flow:/flowIncomplete, so a return with a share still owed reports itself unfinished and names the question; Complete on every input (FED-5695-ALLOCCOMPLETE-045). Line 25c owes a share only when it is taken into account: line 25a Yes, a line 25b code entered whose enabled property qualifies the enabling property.

Fact.Name: Nonbusiness-use percentage for Qualified solar electric property costs (Form 5695 line 1)
Fact.Description: Question: "What percentage of the use of this property is for nonbusiness purposes?", shown beside /writableSolarElectricCosts (Qualified solar electric property costs (Form 5695 line 1)). Help: if less than 80% of the use of an item is for nonbusiness purposes, only the part of its cost allocable to nonbusiness use counts toward the credit (§25D(e)(7); i5695 lines 62-65). Enter a whole percent; enter 100 for property used only for nonbusiness purposes. One percentage applies to every item this entry totals; the graph cannot give items on one entry different percentages. Asked when: /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableSolarElectricCosts is answered. Unanswered: with the gate Yes, the cost this percentage prorates stops resolving (/form5695SolarElectricCostTakenIntoAccount is Incomplete) until it is answered, because the filer has reported business use and the graph must not assume none; with the gate unanswered and the cost above $0 the cost does not resolve whether or not this is given, because the gate itself is the question owed (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered; tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)); with the gate No it is not read. Validation: Int, Min 0, Max 100. Feeds /form5695NonbusinessUseAllocationIsComplete and /form5695SolarElectricCostTakenIntoAccount.

Fact.Name: Cost taken into account after the nonbusiness-use allocation: Qualified solar electric property costs (Form 5695 line 1)
Fact.Description: The amount of /writableSolarElectricCosts that counts toward the credit. When /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableSolarElectricNonbusinessUsePercent is below /form5695NonbusinessUseThresholdPercent (80), the cost times that percentage divided by 100, rounded to the cent at the division (HALF_EVEN, the Dollar type's scale); otherwise the whole entered cost, so at exactly 80 percent the whole cost counts (§25D(e)(7): "less than 80 percent"). With the gate Yes and the percentage unanswered this resolves Incomplete: neither Case matches, so no amount is produced and every reader downstream, through the credit and Schedule 3, is Incomplete too. Complete exactly when /writableSolarElectricCosts is answered and, under a Yes gate, its percentage is too. The allocation is applied to the cost line, ahead of the 30% rate and every dollar cap. Read by /form5695QualifiedCleanEnergyCosts. PER-ITEM ROUTE: when the line 1 item list /form5695Line1SolarElectricItems is supplied, this is the items' costs taken into account added (/form5695Line1SolarElectricItemsAllocatedCost), each item tested for 80 percent nonbusiness use on its own, as section 25D(e)(7) tests each item; the line's single percentage is then not read (FED-5695-NONBUSINESS80-013). GATE UNANSWERED (tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)): with /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse unanswered and a cost above $0, this does not resolve, whether or not a percentage is given, and the return is held (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered): one gate state, one outcome on the typed, printed-box and item-list routes. A $0 or unanswered cost needs no answer.

Fact.Name: Solar electric property costs, floored at zero for Form 5695 line 1 allocation

Unanswered input remains Incomplete; the allocation's own complete-safe branches decide when an absent line contributes $0.

Fact.Name: Nonbusiness-use percentage for Insulation or air sealing material or system costs (Form 5695 line 18a)
Fact.Description: Question: "What percentage of the use of this property is for nonbusiness purposes?", shown beside /writableInsulationCosts (Insulation or air sealing material or system costs (Form 5695 line 18a)). Help: if less than 80% of the use of an item is for nonbusiness purposes, only the part of its cost allocable to nonbusiness use counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1), importing §25D(e)(7); i5695 lines 62-65). Enter a whole percent; enter 100 for property used only for nonbusiness purposes. One percentage applies to every item this entry totals; the graph cannot give items on one entry different percentages. Asked when: /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableInsulationCosts is answered. Unanswered: with the gate Yes, the cost this percentage prorates stops resolving (/form5695InsulationCostTakenIntoAccount is Incomplete) until it is answered, because the filer has reported business use and the graph must not assume none; with the gate No it is not read; with the gate unanswered and the cost above $0 the cost does not resolve whether or not this is given, because the gate itself is the question owed (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered; tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)). Validation: Int, Min 0, Max 100. Feeds /form5695NonbusinessUseAllocationIsComplete and /form5695InsulationCostTakenIntoAccount.

Fact.Name: Cost taken into account after the nonbusiness-use allocation: Insulation or air sealing material or system costs (Form 5695 line 18a)
Fact.Description: The amount of /writableInsulationCosts that counts toward the credit. When /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableInsulationNonbusinessUsePercent is below /form5695NonbusinessUseThresholdPercent (80), the cost times that percentage divided by 100, rounded to the cent at the division (HALF_EVEN, the Dollar type's scale); otherwise the whole entered cost, so at exactly 80 percent the whole cost counts (§25C(f)(1), importing §25D(e)(7): "less than 80 percent"). With the gate Yes and the percentage unanswered this resolves Incomplete: neither Case matches, so no amount is produced and every reader downstream, through the credit and Schedule 3, is Incomplete too. Complete exactly when /writableInsulationCosts is answered and, under a Yes gate, its percentage is too. The allocation is applied to the cost line, ahead of the 30% rate and every dollar cap. Read by /form5695InsulationCredit. SECTION A CLOSED: $0 when line 17a, 17b or 17c is answered No (/form5695SectionAAnsweredNo), because the form leaves lines 18a through 20d blank then (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section A cost waits on an unanswered line 17 question (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section A is closed by an answer. GATE UNANSWERED (tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)): with /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse unanswered and a cost above $0, this does not resolve, whether or not a percentage is given, and the return is held (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered): one gate state, one outcome on the typed, printed-box and item-list routes. A $0 or unanswered cost needs no answer.

PRINTED LINE 19E WITHOUT ITS STATEMENT: the instructions require a statement listing the QMID and cost of each item on line 19e; when /form5695Line19eOtherDoorItems is not supplied, the typed amount /writableLine19eOtherDoorCosts names no item's QMID, so no item on the line is on the return and the printed line 19e is $0, matching the category total and the credit that already exclude it (owner ruling NE-6; section 25C(h)(1)(B)). The statement items, each with its own QMID, are the only route that puts an amount on this line. SECTION A CLOSED: $0 when line 17a, 17b or 17c is answered No (/form5695SectionAAnsweredNo), because the form leaves lines 18a through 20d blank then (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section A cost waits on an unanswered line 17 question (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section A is closed by an answer.

Fact.Name: Nonbusiness-use percentage for Line 20a(i) cost of the first most expensive exterior window or skylight (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: Question: "What percentage of the use of this property is for nonbusiness purposes?", shown beside /writableLine20aEntry1Cost (Line 20a(i) cost of the first most expensive exterior window or skylight (Form 5695 line 20a)). Help: if less than 80% of the use of an item is for nonbusiness purposes, only the part of its cost allocable to nonbusiness use counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1), importing §25D(e)(7); i5695 lines 62-65). Enter a whole percent; enter 100 for property used only for nonbusiness purposes. Asked when: /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableLine20aEntry1Cost is answered. Unanswered: with the gate Yes, the cost this percentage prorates stops resolving (/form5695Line20aEntry1CostTakenIntoAccount is Incomplete) until it is answered, because the filer has reported business use and the graph must not assume none; with the gate No it is not read; with the gate unanswered and the cost above $0 the cost does not resolve whether or not this is given, because the gate itself is the question owed (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered; tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)). Validation: Int, Min 0, Max 100. Feeds /form5695NonbusinessUseAllocationIsComplete and /form5695Line20aEntry1CostTakenIntoAccount.

Fact.Name: Cost taken into account after the nonbusiness-use allocation: Line 20a(i) cost of the first most expensive exterior window or skylight (Form 5695 line 20a)
Fact.Description: The nonnegative amount of /writableLine20aEntry1Cost that counts toward the credit. When /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableLine20aEntry1NonbusinessUsePercent is below /form5695NonbusinessUseThresholdPercent (80), the cost times that percentage divided by 100, rounded to the cent at the division (HALF_EVEN, the Dollar type's scale); otherwise the whole entered cost, so at exactly 80 percent the whole cost counts (§25C(f)(1), importing §25D(e)(7): "less than 80 percent"). With the gate Yes and the percentage unanswered this resolves Incomplete: neither Case matches, so no amount is produced and every reader downstream, through the credit and Schedule 3, is Incomplete too. Complete exactly when /writableLine20aEntry1Cost is answered and, under a Yes gate, its percentage is too. The allocation is applied to the cost line, ahead of the 30% rate and every dollar cap. Read by /form5695Line20aEntry1CostOrZero. NO QMID, NO AMOUNT: an item whose own Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number is not entered in the QMID box printed on line 20a(i) (/writableLine20aEntry1QmidFirst4) is not on the return, so section 25C(h)(1)(B) allows no credit for it and this printed line 20a(i) amount is $0 (FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048, FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046; owner ruling NE-6: $0, not a refusal). An unprinted category-level QMID intake does not substitute for the printed box. SECTION A CLOSED: $0 when line 17a, 17b or 17c is answered No (/form5695SectionAAnsweredNo), because the form leaves lines 18a through 20d blank then (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section A cost waits on an unanswered line 17 question (/form5695SectionAQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section A is closed by an answer. GATE UNANSWERED (tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)): with /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse unanswered and a cost above $0, this does not resolve, whether or not a percentage is given, and the return is held (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered): one gate state, one outcome on the typed, printed-box and item-list routes. A $0 or unanswered cost needs no answer.

When /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableLine23aEntry2NonbusinessUsePercent is below /form5695NonbusinessUseThresholdPercent (80), the cost times that percentage divided by 100, rounded to the cent at the division (HALF_EVEN, the Dollar type's scale); otherwise the whole entered cost, so at exactly 80 percent the whole cost counts (§25C(f)(1), importing §25D(e)(7): "less than 80 percent"). With the gate Yes and the percentage unanswered this resolves Incomplete: neither Case matches, so no amount is produced and every reader downstream, through the credit and Schedule 3, is Incomplete too. Complete exactly when /writableLine23aEntry2Cost is answered and, under a Yes gate, its percentage is too. The allocation is applied to the cost line, ahead of the 30% rate and every dollar cap. Read by /form5695Line23aEntry2CostOrZero. NO QMID, NO AMOUNT: an item whose own Qualified Manufacturer Identification Number is not entered in the QMID box printed on line 23a(ii) (/writableLine23aEntry2QmidFirst4) is not on the return, so section 25C(h)(1)(B) allows no credit for it and this printed line 23a(ii) amount is $0 (FED-5695-P2-PRINTEDQMID-048, FED-5695-P2-HEADERQMID-046; owner ruling NE-6: $0, not a refusal). An unprinted category-level QMID intake does not substitute for the printed box. SECTION B CLOSED: $0 when line 21a or 21b is answered No (/form5695SectionBAnsweredNo), because the form says to skip lines 22 through 25 and line 29 then (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section B cost waits on an unanswered line 21 question (/form5695SectionBQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section B is closed by an answer. GATE UNANSWERED (tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)): with /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse unanswered and a cost above $0, this does not resolve, whether or not a percentage is given, and the return is held (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered): one gate state, one outcome on the typed, printed-box and item-list routes. A $0 or unanswered cost needs no answer.

Fact.Name: Nonbusiness-use percentage for Cost of all other natural gas, propane, or oil water heaters (Form 5695 line 23b)
Fact.Description: Question: "What percentage of the use of this property is for nonbusiness purposes?", shown beside /writableLine23bOtherWaterHeaterCosts (Cost of all other natural gas, propane, or oil water heaters (Form 5695 line 23b)). NOT ASKED AND NOT READ: the typed line 23b amount it would prorate adds $0 on every return, because a typed amount with no statement names no item's QMID (section 25C(h)(1)(B); tax interpretation IN-271), and an allocation is owed only for a cost taken into account (section 25D(e)(7)). The line 23b statement items carry their own nonbusiness-use shares. Kept so saved returns load. Validation: Int, Min 0, Max 100.

Fact.Name: Cost taken into account after the nonbusiness-use allocation: Cost of all other natural gas, propane, or oil water heaters (Form 5695 line 23b)
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 23b as printed: the line 23b statement's costs taken into account, item by item with each item's QMID and its own nonbusiness-use share, when the statement is supplied; $0 for a typed line 23b amount with no statement. A selected incomplete or contradictory statement does not resolve. PRINTED LINE 23B WITHOUT ITS STATEMENT: the instructions require a statement listing the QMID and cost of each item on line 23b; when /form5695Line23bOtherWaterHeaterItems is not supplied, the typed amount /writableLine23bOtherWaterHeaterCosts names no item's QMID, so no item on the line is on the return and the printed line 23b is $0, matching the category total and the credit that already exclude it (owner ruling NE-6; section 25C(h)(1)(B)). The statement items, each with its own QMID, are the only route that puts an amount on this line. SECTION B CLOSED: $0 when line 21a or 21b is answered No (/form5695SectionBAnsweredNo), because the form says to skip lines 22 through 25 and line 29 then (FED-5695-P2-JOINTOCCGATE-050). ONE GATE TEST (IN-277): does not resolve while a Section B cost waits on an unanswered line 21 question (/form5695SectionBQuestionsAnswered); $0 once Section B is closed by an answer.

Fact.Name: Nonbusiness-use percentage for Cost of the most expensive natural gas, propane, or oil furnace or hot water boiler (Form 5695 line 24a)
Fact.Description: Question: "What percentage of the use of this property is for nonbusiness purposes?", shown beside /writableLine24aFurnaceBoilerCost (Cost of the most expensive natural gas, propane, or oil furnace or hot water boiler (Form 5695 line 24a)). Help: if less than 80% of the use of an item is for nonbusiness purposes, only the part of its cost allocable to nonbusiness use counts toward the credit (§25C(f)(1), importing §25D(e)(7); i5695 lines 62-65). Enter a whole percent; enter 100 for property used only for nonbusiness purposes. Asked when: /writableForm5695AnyItemUnder80PercentNonbusinessUse is Yes and /writableLine24aFurnaceBoilerCost is answered. Unanswered: with the gate Yes, the cost this percentage prorates stops resolving (/form5695Line24aFurnaceBoilerCostTakenIntoAccount is Incomplete) until it is answered, because the filer has reported business use and the graph must not assume none; with the gate No it is not read; with the gate unanswered and the cost above $0 the cost does not resolve whether or not this is given, because the gate itself is the question owed (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered; tax interpretation IN-277 (e), (i)). Validation: Int, Min 0, Max 100. Feeds /form5695NonbusinessUseAllocationIsComplete and /form5695Line24aFurnaceBoilerCostTakenIntoAccount.
