Fact.Name: Form 5695 is required for this return
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Form 5695, and it must cover BOTH parts: "Use Form 5695 to figure and take your residential energy credits" (Instructions for Form 5695, Purpose of Form) names one form for two credits — Part I, the residential clean energy credit (Schedule 3 line 5a), and Part II, the energy efficient home improvement credit (Schedule 3 line 5b). Gating on Part I alone would silently drop every return whose only Form 5695 claim is a Part II improvement.
PART I is /residentialCleanEnergyPartIIsActive, which already exists and already states the input test (the five line 1-5 cost categories, the line 8 fuel cell cost, the line 12 carryforward from 2024). It is deliberately Part I only, because its other consumer — ctcOdc:/isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB — reads Credit Limit Worksheet A line 3 bullet c, which names Form 5695 PART I; that fact is reused here, not widened, so the worksheet consumer is untouched.
PART II is the twelve input predicates this module already carries for the Part II cost lines: the eight line-level roll-ups (/form5695Line19fOtherDoorCostsAnswered, /form5695Line20cWindowSkylightCostsAnswered, /form5695Line22cCentralAcCostsAnswered, /form5695Line23cFossilFuelWaterHeaterCostsAnswered, /form5695Line24cFurnaceBoilerCostsAnswered, /form5695Line29HeatPumpCostsAnswered, /form5695Line29HeatPumpWaterHeaterCostsAnswered, /form5695Line29BiomassCostsAnswered), each of which already reads "the components or the typed total", plus the four Part II cost lines that have no roll-up of their own: insulation, the home energy audit, the most expensive exterior door, and the enabling property costs. TWO MAIN HOMES: also when the two-main-homes rule applies on a joint return (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesApplies), because this form's line 30 then carries the other home's line 30 even with no cost on this home, and step 4 attaches both forms (i5695 lines 190-196; tax interpretation IN-277 (g)); and while the two-homes question is unanswered with the other home's line 30 entered (/form5695MfjTwoMainHomesAnsweredWhenOtherHomeLine30Entered FALSE), when the return is held and the form may be owed (IN-277 (d)).
AN INPUT TEST, NOT A VALUE TEST, in the shape /residentialCleanEnergyPartIIsActive set and for the same reason: a Part II claim can be reduced to $0 by the section 25C annual limits or by the tax-liability limit and the filer still files the form that shows the computation. Complete-safe by construction — every leg is an Answered predicate or an IsComplete, so this resolves Complete on every return, which is what a render gate needs.

Fact.Name: Basis-point scale for item use
Fact.Description: One percentage point is 100 basis points. Thus 10000 represents 100% nonbusiness use; this scale is not a tax rate.

Fact.Name: Nonbusiness-use threshold in basis points
Fact.Description: At 8000 basis points (80%) the whole eligible cost counts; below that threshold only the nonbusiness share counts.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 1 items, each with its own nonbusiness-use share
Fact.Description: One item for each separate item of qualified solar electric property whose cost is included on Form 5695 line 1, across every home the filer used as a residence. Supply this list when any item on the line is used less than 80 percent for nonbusiness purposes and the items' uses differ: the 80 percent test and the allocation apply to each item separately, which one percentage for the whole line cannot express. When the list is supplied, line 1 takes into account each item's whole cost when the item's nonbusiness use is at least 80 percent, and only its nonbusiness portion otherwise; the line's own percentage is not read. The line's typed whole cost /writableSolarElectricCosts is optional with the list; if it is answered it must equal the sum of the items' whole costs. An unanswered list keeps the single-percentage route.

Fact.Name: This item's whole cost on Form 5695 line 1
Fact.Description: The whole cost of this one item of qualified solar electric property included on Form 5695 line 1, before any nonbusiness-use allocation, including the labor costs the line includes. Do not enter an already-allocated cost. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed; for a reconstructed home, when your original use of it begins; for a newly constructed home, when your original use of it begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. SUBSIDIES: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf.

Fact.Name: This item's nonbusiness-use share, in basis points
Fact.Description: The share of this item's use that is for nonbusiness purposes, in hundredths of a percent: enter 10000 for 100%, 8000 for exactly 80%, 7000 for 70%. At 8000 or more the whole cost counts; below 8000 only that share of the cost counts. A positive cost requires an answer; a zero-cost item does not.

Fact.Name: This item's cost taken into account after the 80 percent test
Fact.Description: The part of this item's cost that counts on Form 5695 line 1: the whole cost when its nonbusiness-use share is at least 80 percent; otherwise the cost times the share in basis points divided by 10,000 (multiply before dividing; Dollar arithmetic rounds at cents). $0 for a zero-cost item. A positive cost with no share answered does not resolve. With the business-use question answered No (no item used less than 80 percent for nonbusiness purposes) and no share given, the whole cost counts (section 25D(e)(7)); with it Yes or unanswered a positive cost needs its share. With the 80 percent nonbusiness-use question unanswered, a positive cost does not resolve even with its share given, and the return is held (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered; tax interpretation IN-277 (i)).

Fact.Name: The Form 5695 line 1 item list is supplied
Fact.Description: True when /form5695Line1SolarElectricItems is answered (an explicitly empty list included); line 1 then takes its cost from the items, each tested for 80 percent nonbusiness use on its own.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 1 items: whole costs added
Fact.Description: The items' whole costs added, before any nonbusiness-use allocation; it must equal the line's whole cost /writableSolarElectricCosts.

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 1 items: costs taken into account added
Fact.Description: The amount Form 5695 line 1 takes into account when the item list is supplied: each item's cost taken into account after its own 80 percent test, added. The items give the amounts paid that the line asks for (i5695 line 273), so with the line's typed whole cost unanswered the items alone decide; a typed whole cost that differs from the items' whole costs added leaves the line unresolved and holds the return (/form5695PartIItemListsMatchLineTotals), and an item missing its share leaves it unresolved too.

Fact.Name: Line 19e complete all-other item statement

With the collection unanswered the line b amount is $0: the typed line b amount names no item's QMID and adds $0 (tax interpretation IN-271). An explicitly empty collection states there are no all-other items. A populated collection selects exact per-item allocation and QMID validation; supply the inventory-complete confirmation. This is a source register, not document extraction.

Fact.Name: Line 19e item statement is complete
Fact.Description: Confirm that /form5695Line19eOtherDoorItems contains every item on line 19e, with no duplicates or costs already included in printed item boxes. Costs must meet the line-specific 2025 property/installation requirements, exclude disallowed labor for doors/windows, reflect subsidies as applicable to Part II, and be amounts actually paid by this filer. A false or unanswered confirmation leaves a populated statement incomplete.

Fact.Name: Line 19e detailed statement selected
Fact.Description: An explicitly supplied collection or its inventory-confirmation answer selects detailed mode. A confirmation without a collection must not be treated as a return with no statement.

Fact.Name: Qualifying item cost before business-use allocation
Fact.Description: The whole eligible cost of this one item on line 19e, before the nonbusiness-use allocation, but after required Part II rebates/subsidy adjustments. Do not enter a category total or an already-allocated cost. Qualification depends on the specific property standard and installation during 2025; a syntactically valid QMID alone does not establish qualification. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. So a cost paid this year for an installation completed next year does not belong here, and a cost paid last year for an installation completed this year does. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. CONDOMINIUM OR COOPERATIVE: a member of a condominium management association for a condominium you own, or a tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation, is treated as having paid a proportionate share of the association or corporation costs; include that share here. SUBSIDIES AND FINANCING: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf, and exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing (financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or energy-production projects). STANDARD: the door must meet the applicable Energy Star requirements.

Fact.Name: This item nonbusiness-use share, in basis points
Fact.Description: Enter 10000 for 100%, 8000 for exactly 80%, or 5000 for 50%. Values range from 0 to 10000, allowing increments of 0.01 percentage point. The threshold is applied separately to this item. A positive cost requires an answer; a zero-cost row does not.

Fact.Name: This item manufacturer QMID
Fact.Description: The four-character alphanumeric QMID supplied by the qualified manufacturer for this specific 2025 item. It is not borrowed from another item or the category header. This validates the format, not the issuer against an external manufacturer database. Keep any longer product identifier separately in supporting records.

Fact.Name: This item cost after the 80% test
Fact.Description: For a positive qualifying cost, require this item QMID and nonbusiness-use share. Below 80%, multiply cost by the basis-point share before dividing by 10000; at or above 80%, use the whole cost. Dollar arithmetic rounds at cents, HALF_EVEN. Missing required information remains Incomplete. A zero-cost row contributes zero without irrelevant answers. An item with a positive cost and no QMID counts $0 and the rest of the statement still computes (section 25C(h)(1)(B); tax interpretation IN-271); it does not hold the return. With the business-use question answered No (no item used less than 80 percent for nonbusiness purposes) and no share given, the whole cost counts (section 25D(e)(7)); with it Yes or unanswered a positive cost needs its share. Fact.Name: One when a positive-cost item has less than 80% nonbusiness use

Fact.Name: Statement whole-cost total
Fact.Description: Sum the whole costs actually paid for the item inventory, before business-use allocation.

Fact.Name: Statement individually allocated cost total

Fact.Name: Statement sources and any scalar total reconcile
Fact.Description: A populated statement needs a complete-inventory confirmation and complete whole/allocated totals. A supplied old all-other scalar must equal the WHOLE cost total, never the allocated total. An explicit return-level No to any under-80 item contradicts a positive-cost under-80 statement item. Empty statements need no confirmation but cannot coexist with a nonzero typed line b amount.

Fact.Name: Reconciled all-other statement cost
Fact.Description: Only a ready detailed statement supplies the all-other cost. An unconfirmed or conflicting selected statement remains Incomplete; it never falls back to the typed line b amount or to zero.

Fact.Name: Category whole-cost reconciliation total
Fact.Description: Whole costs in the preceding itemized boxes plus this all-other statement. Used only to check a simultaneously supplied typed line b amount or typed category total; it is not the business-use-adjusted credit base.

Fact.Name: Category item identities and typed total reconcile
Fact.Description: If an old typed category total is supplied, it must equal the whole-cost inventory. No QMID is requested for an unused or zero-cost preceding box. Fact.Name: Qualified category cost for a selected statement
Fact.Description: Use the existing category total only when the detailed statement and preceding item QMIDs reconcile. A known ineligible section contributes zero; unresolved selected source information does not silently become zero.

Fact.Name: This other door credit before the all-door ceiling
Fact.Description: 30% of this item eligible allocated cost, limited to $250 per exterior door. This remains at cents before the aggregate credit is rounded and subjected to the $500 all-door limit.

Fact.Name: Other statement doors credit before the all-door ceiling
Fact.Description: Sum each separate door credit after its $250 cap. Do not cap only the total cost while allowing a single door to exceed its item ceiling.

Fact.Name: All other doors credit with individual item ceilings
Fact.Description: For the selected all-other statement, combine individually capped credits from the two printed additional-door boxes and the statement rows. Round the aggregate once; the existing all-door reader then applies the $500 combined limit.

Fact.Name: Line 20b complete all-other item statement
Fact.Description: One item for each separate qualifying property included ONLY on Form 5695 line 20b. Do not repeat an item reported in a preceding printed box or another statement. This is a source register, not document extraction.

Fact.Name: Line 20b item statement is complete

Fact.Name: Line 20b detailed statement selected
Fact.Description: An explicitly supplied collection or its inventory-confirmation answer selects detailed mode. A confirmation without a collection must not be treated as a return with no statement.

Fact.Name: Qualifying item cost before business-use allocation
Fact.Description: The whole eligible cost of this one item on line 20b, before the nonbusiness-use allocation, but after required Part II rebates/subsidy adjustments. Do not enter a category total or an already-allocated cost. Qualification depends on the specific property standard and installation during 2025; a syntactically valid QMID alone does not establish qualification. WHEN A COST COUNTS: a cost is treated as paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, for costs connected with reconstructing your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins. SHARED WITH A NEIGHBOR: if you and a neighbor shared the cost of property that benefits each of your main homes, enter only the part of the cost you paid; the credit limits apply to each of you separately. SUBSIDIES AND FINANCING: enter this cost net of any public-utility subsidy for the property that was not included in your gross income, including a subsidy received by a contractor on your behalf, and exclude any amount financed by subsidized energy financing (financing under a federal, state, or local program whose main purpose is to fund energy-conservation or energy-production projects). STANDARD: the property must meet or exceed the highest efficiency tier (not including any advanced tier) established by the Consortium for Energy Efficiency that is in effect at the beginning of the calendar year in which it is placed in service.

Fact.Name: This item nonbusiness-use share, in basis points
Fact.Description: Enter 10000 for 100%, 8000 for exactly 80%, or 5000 for 50%. Values range from 0 to 10000, allowing increments of 0.01 percentage point. The threshold is applied separately to this item. A positive cost requires an answer; a zero-cost row does not.

Fact.Name: This item manufacturer QMID
Fact.Description: The four-character alphanumeric QMID supplied by the qualified manufacturer for this specific 2025 item. It is not borrowed from another item or the category header. This validates the format, not the issuer against an external manufacturer database. Keep any longer product identifier separately in supporting records.

Fact.Name: This item cost after the 80% test
Fact.Description: For a positive qualifying cost, require this item QMID and nonbusiness-use share. Below 80%, multiply cost by the basis-point share before dividing by 10000; at or above 80%, use the whole cost. Dollar arithmetic rounds at cents, HALF_EVEN. Missing required information remains Incomplete. A zero-cost row contributes zero without irrelevant answers. An item with a positive cost and no QMID counts $0 and the rest of the statement still computes (section 25C(h)(1)(B); tax interpretation IN-271); it does not hold the return. With the business-use question answered No (no item used less than 80 percent for nonbusiness purposes) and no share given, the whole cost counts (section 25D(e)(7)); with it Yes or unanswered a positive cost needs its share. With the 80 percent nonbusiness-use question unanswered, a positive cost does not resolve even with its share given, and the return is held (/form5695BusinessUseQuestionAnsweredWhenCostEntered; tax interpretation IN-277 (i)).

Fact.Name: One when a positive-cost item has less than 80% nonbusiness use
Fact.Description: A numeric indicator for reconciling the existing return-level business-use answer. This is not an expense or a credit. An item with no share answered is not counted as under 80 percent (its cost line handles the missing share).

Fact.Name: Statement individually allocated cost total

Fact.Name: Qualified category cost for a selected statement

Fact.Name: Joint fuel-cell cost worksheet selected
Fact.Description: True when line 7c is checked and the return is not a joint return: the joint-occupancy rules do not apply to married individuals filing a joint return (i5695 line 128), so on a joint return line 8 is figured without the allocation even when line 7c is checked (FED-5695-P1-JOINTOCC-037).

Fact.Name: Whether line 7c's joint-occupancy rule applies is known
Fact.Description: True when line 7c is not checked, or the filing status is known (the rule does not apply on a joint return). False while line 7c is checked and the filing status is unanswered: line 8 then waits rather than assuming either way (FED-5695-P1-JOINTOCC-037).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 7c is answered whenever a joint-occupancy worksheet amount is entered
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when line 7c (/writableLine7cJointOccupantsRule, a check box) is unanswered while line 8 carries a fuel cell amount and an all-occupants joint-occupancy amount (/writableFuelCellJointAllOccupantsCosts) is entered above $0, line 7a is not answered No, and the return is not known to be a joint return. Line 8, and so lines 9 through 11, then do not resolve, rather than figuring line 8 as if the joint-occupancy rule did not apply. TRUE otherwise: an unanswered line 7c with no worksheet amount is the unchecked box and computes; on a joint return the rule does not apply (i5695 line 128) and nothing is held (tax interpretation IN-277 (c)).

Fact.Name: All occupants qualifying fuel-cell costs
Fact.Description: Total qualifying whole costs paid by this filer and all other occupants for the SAME single fuel-cell installation. Include this filer share. This is not merely the other occupants share and is not a tax-credit amount.

Fact.Name: Nameplate capacity of the shared fuel-cell installation, watts
Fact.Description: Nameplate electrical capacity in whole watts; under 500 W counts no half kilowatt, so line 10 and the cost ceiling are $0 (the form: if less than 0.5 kW, enter -0-). For example, 5 kW is 5000 watts. Supply the same property capacity used by all occupants; do not enter an ownership-proportioned capacity.

Fact.Name: Single shared fuel-cell property scope confirmed
Fact.Description: Confirm one qualifying fuel-cell installation at the filer main home in the United States, put in service in 2025, with at least 80% nonbusiness use, eligible costs and no pooling of separate installations or other main homes. The cost sources must already exclude ineligible storage/pool amounts. This route does not apply to spouses filing jointly or to a below-80% mixed-use installation. A confirmation is not automatic verification of omitted records.

Fact.Name: Maximum fuel-cell cost available to all joint occupants
Fact.Description: For the single shared property, $1,667 for each WHOLE half kilowatt of capacity: the capacity in watts is first taken down to a multiple of 500 (1,300 W counts as 1,000 W, two half kilowatts), then $1,667 x watts / 500. This is the combined QUALIFYING COST limit for all occupants, not the credit limit. Use the statutory $1,667 figure, not $1,666.67. A part of a half kilowatt adds nothing, because the ceiling is stated per half kilowatt and the instructions allow capacity only in half kW increments (FED-5695-P1-JOINTOCC-037). A capacity under 500 watts counts as zero half kilowatts, so this is $0, as the form says to enter -0- under 0.5 kW (FED-5695-P1-JOINTOCC-037).

Fact.Name: Fuel-cell capacity credit limit
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 10 for the joint-occupancy worksheet: $500 for each WHOLE half kilowatt of the same property's capacity, which is $1 per watt after the capacity is taken down to a multiple of 500 watts (1,300 W gives $1,000, not $1,300). The allocated cost is separately limited before the 30% rate (FED-5695-P1-FUELCELLKW-039). A capacity under 500 watts counts as zero half kilowatts, so this is $0, as the form says to enter -0- under 0.5 kW (FED-5695-P1-JOINTOCC-037).

Fact.Name: Joint fuel-cell sources are consistent
Fact.Description: The joint-occupancy worksheet can be figured: line 7c applies off a joint return, line 7a is Yes, and the inputs are complete and consistent (/form5695FuelCellJointWorksheetInputsComplete). A typed line 10 amount is not compared: the capacity in watts decides line 10 (tax interpretation IN-275). The nonbusiness share is not a gate here: section 25D(e)(7) applies first, through /form5695Line8FuelCellCostBeforeJointOccupancy (IN-274) (FED-5695-P1-JOINTOCC-037).

Fact.Name: Fuel-cell joint-occupancy cost allocable to this filer
Fact.Description: Line 8 under line 7c: the smaller of this occupant's own figure (/form5695Line8FuelCellCostBeforeJointOccupancy, already limited to its nonbusiness part under section 25D(e)(7)) and the all-occupant ceiling ($1,667 per whole half kilowatt) times that own figure divided by the own figure plus what the other occupants paid (section 25D(e)(4)(B); tax interpretations IN-273, IN-274). Multiply before dividing; the Dollar division rounds to the cent. Does not resolve while the worksheet is held (/form5695FuelCellJointWorksheetInputsComplete).

Fact.Name: Applied line 10 capacity credit ceiling for print
Fact.Description: The amount printed on Form 5695 line 10: the computed capacity ceiling on the selected joint worksheet, otherwise the line 10 amount from the printed kilowatt boxes or the typed amount, each in whole half kilowatts at $500 (/form5695Line10LimitOrZero). It does not resolve, and so prints blank, when no capacity is answered. This is not a separate credit or a replacement for the whole/fractional kW source boxes (FED-5695-P1-FUELCELLKW-039).

Fact.Name: Form 5695 line 10 from the printed kilowatt boxes, in whole half kilowatts
Fact.Description: Form 5695 line 10 figured from the two printed capacity boxes, /writableLine10KilowattCapacityWholeNumber (whole kilowatts) and /writableLine10KilowattCapacityDecimals (the digits after the decimal point). The capacity counts only in whole half kilowatts: each whole kilowatt is $1,000 (two half kilowatts at $500), and the decimal part adds $500 only when it is at least .5 (its first digit is 5 through 9), so 1.3 kW gives $1,000 and 2.5 kW gives $2,500. A capacity under 0.5 kW gives $0, as the form says to enter -0-. Complete when either box is answered (an unanswered whole-number box beside an answered decimal box reads as 0 kW); otherwise it does not resolve, and line 10 falls back to /writableLine10KilowattCapacityLimit. FED-5695-P1-FUELCELLKW-039.

Fact.Name: A Form 5695 line 10 printed capacity box is answered
Fact.Description: True when either printed capacity box of line 10, /writableLine10KilowattCapacityWholeNumber or /writableLine10KilowattCapacityDecimals, is answered; line 10 is then figured from the boxes (/form5695Line10CapacityFromPrintedKilowatts).

Fact.Name: The typed Form 5695 line 10 amount taken down to whole half kilowatts
Fact.Description: The filer-typed line 10 amount /writableLine10KilowattCapacityLimit (kW capacity x $1,000), not below $0, taken down to a multiple of $500, because the credit counts capacity only in whole half kilowatts ($500 each): a typed $1,300 (1.3 kW) is $1,000. Read only when neither printed capacity box is answered. FED-5695-P1-FUELCELLKW-039.

Fact.Description: Whole-dollar observation of the sum of exact individual door allocations. The category calculation retains the exact unrounded total until after applying any household payment-share ceiling.

Fact.Description: An entered all-door other-payment total of zero establishes missing individual answers as zero only when no entered individual door payment contradicts zero. Explicit payments are retained; this inference never overwrites positive or negative inputs.

Fact.Name: Exact constituent other-payment total for qualifying exterior doors
Fact.Description: Sum complete other-occupant payments on qualifying doors toward which this filer paid. These corresponding-property payments serve the line 28 denominator. Add the separate other-only inventory for the door-category household denominator; the optional legacy all-door total cross-checks that broader household total.

Fact.Name: Qualifying main-door cost used by the individual allocation
Fact.Description: An unused or nonpositive main-door cost contributes zero without asking for irrelevant door details. A positive entered main-door cost reads its existing qualifying cost, preserving its unknown required qualification or business-use answers as Incomplete.

Fact.Name: All qualifying household exterior doors are accounted for
Fact.Description: With line 32a checked and positive own qualifying door costs, confirm that the listed own-payment doors plus the separate other-occupants-only door inventory cover every qualifying exterior door for this home and tax year, without duplicates. Include doors paid entirely by other occupants. False or unanswered confirmation leaves the new inventory incomplete. New interviews derive totals and do not ask for a typed all-door aggregate.

Fact.Name: Qualifying exterior doors paid entirely by other occupants
Fact.Description: One row per physical qualifying exterior door for this home and tax year that you paid nothing toward. Exclude every door already on your lines 19a, 19d or 19e. Include only eligible 2025 doors with required manufacturer identification and qualifying-use evidence; retain that evidence with the allocation statement. An explicitly empty list states there are none; confirm the complete household inventory separately. These rows affect the household door-category limit, never your own printed cost or line 28 corresponding-property denominator.

Fact.Name: Other occupants qualifying payment for this door
Fact.Description: Total qualifying payment by all other occupants for this single physical door, after rebates, excluded installation labor, subsidies and each payer's applicable nonbusiness-use adjustment. The filer paid zero. Enter only costs of a qualifying installed door with manufacturer identification evidence. A missing or negative amount is invalid and holds the household allocation. Do not combine multiple doors in one row.

Fact.Name: Validated qualifying other-only door payment
Fact.Description: Read a complete nonnegative eligible payment; a missing or negative payment remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Household credit for an other-only door before the all-door ceiling
Fact.Description: Apply the 30 percent rate and the individual 250 dollar ceiling to this qualifying door before deciding whether household credits exceed the 500 dollar all-door limit.

Fact.Name: Other-only door qualifying payments
Fact.Description: Sum the complete other-only inventory after household confirmation. When neither new inventory input is supplied, expose zero solely for legacy reconciliation; readiness still requires a matching legacy household aggregate. A partially supplied new inventory never falls back to legacy.

Fact.Name: Other-only door household credit before the category ceiling
Fact.Description: Sum individually capped credits, without whole-dollar rounding, for all qualifying doors paid entirely by other occupants. A partially supplied new inventory remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: All other occupants household door payments
Fact.Description: Sum other-occupant payments on the filer's qualifying doors and on the separate other-only inventory. This household scope is used by the door category allocation and the optional legacy cross-check. The line 28 corresponding-property denominator continues to use only the filer's corresponding doors.

Fact.Name: Household door inventory and optional total agree
Fact.Description: True only when required per-door payments are complete, and either the new complete household inventory is confirmed or a legacy aggregate establishes there are no additional other-only doors. With an attested complete new inventory, an optional legacy total must reconcile to all household other payments within less than one dollar. Without new inventory inputs, exact equality is required to infer that no other-only door is missing; a sub-dollar residual can cross the household credit trigger. New interviews derive this total; a total alone cannot establish how many additional doors there are.

Fact.Name: Household credit for this door before the category ceiling
Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar ceiling to 30 percent of all qualifying payments for this same physical door. Preserve cents; do not round this household trigger to whole dollars. An unused own-payment slot contributes zero; other-only doors belong in the separate household inventory.

Fact.Name: Household credit for this door before the category ceiling
Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar ceiling to 30 percent of all qualifying payments for this same physical door. Preserve cents; do not round this household trigger to whole dollars. An unused own-payment slot contributes zero; other-only doors belong in the separate household inventory.

Fact.Name: Household credit for this door before the category ceiling
Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar ceiling to 30 percent of all qualifying payments for this same physical door. Preserve cents; do not round this household trigger to whole dollars. An unused own-payment slot contributes zero; other-only doors belong in the separate household inventory.

Fact.Name: Household credit for this door before the category ceiling
Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar ceiling to 30 percent of all qualifying payments for this same physical door. Preserve cents; do not round this household trigger to whole dollars. An unused own-payment slot contributes zero; other-only doors belong in the separate household inventory.

Fact.Name: Household credits for the filer statement doors
Fact.Description: Sum per-door capped household credits for a complete selected statement; an unselected statement contributes zero.

Fact.Name: Household door credit after individual limits and before the category limit
Fact.Description: Sum the individually capped household credits for every qualifying door, including doors paid entirely by other occupants. The category allocation applies only when this unrounded total exceeds 500 dollars. Equality does not trigger allocation.

Fact.Name: Exact allocated credit for this exterior door
Fact.Description: Keep the same-door payment fraction exact through the individual cap. Do not round this hidden contribution; round only the final printed line. Missing required payment or qualification information remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Exact normal credit for this exterior door
Fact.Description: Apply the 30 percent rate and 250 dollar individual cap to this physical door before the all-door limit, independently of input ordering. Keep fractional cents until the final printed line.

Fact.Name: Exact household credit for this exterior door
Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar cap to all qualifying payments for this door without rounding. This amount participates in the strict household 500 dollar trigger, so even a subcent amount can matter.

Fact.Name: Exact allocated credit for this exterior door
Fact.Description: Keep the same-door payment fraction exact through the individual cap. Do not round this hidden contribution; round only the final printed line. Missing required payment or qualification information remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Exact household credit for this exterior door
Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar cap to all qualifying payments for this door without rounding. This amount participates in the strict household 500 dollar trigger, so even a subcent amount can matter.

Fact.Name: Exact allocated credit for this exterior door
Fact.Description: Keep the same-door payment fraction exact through the individual cap. Do not round this hidden contribution; round only the final printed line. Missing required payment or qualification information remains Incomplete.

Fact.Description: Apply the 30 percent rate and 250 dollar individual cap to this physical door before the all-door limit, independently of input ordering. Keep fractional cents until the final printed line.

Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar cap to all qualifying payments for this door without rounding. This amount participates in the strict household 500 dollar trigger, so even a subcent amount can matter.

Fact.Name: Exact household credit for this exterior door
Fact.Description: Apply the individual 250 dollar cap to all qualifying payments for this door without rounding. This amount participates in the strict household 500 dollar trigger, so even a subcent amount can matter.

Fact.Name: Exact statement-door total
Fact.Description: An unselected statement contributes zero. A selected statement must be complete and reconciled; sum exact item contributions without cent or whole-dollar rounding.

Fact.Name: Exact statement-door total
Fact.Description: An unselected statement contributes zero. A selected statement must be complete and reconciled; sum exact item contributions without cent or whole-dollar rounding.

Fact.Name: Exact statement-door total
Fact.Description: An unselected statement contributes zero. A selected statement must be complete and reconciled; sum exact item contributions without cent or whole-dollar rounding.

Fact.Name: Exact total of individual door credits
Fact.Description: Add each physical door contribution before rounding or applying the all-door ceiling. Printed slots and statement items use the same per-item limit.

Fact.Name: Exact total of individual door credits
Fact.Description: Add each physical door contribution before rounding or applying the all-door ceiling. Printed slots and statement items use the same per-item limit.

Fact.Name: Individual door credits before the all-door cap
Fact.Description: Whole-dollar observation of the exact normal per-door sum. The final category calculation reads the exact total, not this display value.

Fact.Name: Exact household credit for a door paid entirely by others
Fact.Description: Apply the individual cap to this qualifying physical door without rounding, including fractional cents in the household category trigger.

Fact.Name: Exact household credit for other-only doors
Fact.Description: Use every confirmed qualifying other-only door; missing new inventory inputs remain incomplete. The legacy route supplies zero only when the separate readiness check establishes no additional doors.

Fact.Name: Exact household credit after the individual door limits
Fact.Description: Sum exact individually capped household credits before the all-door limit. Compare this fraction directly with 500: 500.003 exceeds 500 even though a cent or whole-dollar display would be 500.

Fact.Name: The exact household door total exceeds 500 dollars
Fact.Description: The category payment-share ceiling applies only when the complete household sum after per-door caps strictly exceeds 500 dollars. No cent conversion or whole-dollar rounding precedes the comparison.

Fact.Name: Exact household door category share
Fact.Description: Apply the household 500 dollar ceiling using the filer eligible payments over all occupants eligible payments for every qualifying household door. This share cannot increase the filer individual-door credits. It is used only when the exact household trigger exceeds 500.

Fact.Name: Door allocation statement required
Fact.Description: A confirmed joint-occupancy door claim requires the line 32a allocation explanation. The same computation report may also explain a statutory per-door adjustment when the ordinary printed shortcut differs from the capped result.

Fact.Name: Door computation statement required
Fact.Description: Provide the joint allocation statement when required, a cost and QMID statement for positive line 19e items, and a computation explanation whenever independent statutory per-door caps make line 19h differ from the ordinary printed subtotal. This output selects a report; the renderer performs no tax arithmetic.

Fact.Name: Input position for printed door rank 1
Fact.Description: Rank the three individually entered doors by qualifying cost after the nonbusiness-use adjustment. Equal costs retain their original entry order. An unknown required qualifying cost leaves the order unresolved. Itemized statement doors remain on line 19e.

Fact.Name: Input position for printed door rank 3
Fact.Description: Rank the three individually entered doors by qualifying cost after the nonbusiness-use adjustment. Equal costs retain their original entry order. An unknown required qualifying cost leaves the order unresolved. Itemized statement doors remain on line 19e.

Fact.Name: Input position for the second printed door
Fact.Description: The middle input position is the remaining member of the three distinct positions zero, one and two after selecting the highest and lowest qualifying costs. Stable ties preserve physical-door identity.

Fact.Name: Qualifying cost for printed door rank 1
Fact.Description: Print the qualifying cost of this physical door in descending cost order among the three individually entered doors. The manufacturer number and allocated credit follow the same physical door; statement inventory stays on line 19e.

Fact.Name: Manufacturer number for printed door rank 1: first four QMID characters
Fact.Description: Keep this manufacturer-number segment paired with its physical door when qualifying costs are reordered. An absent optional segment prints blank and does not prevent the cost or credit from resolving. A door with no qualifying cost prints no manufacturer number.

Fact.Description: Keep this manufacturer-number segment paired with its physical door when qualifying costs are reordered. An absent optional segment prints blank and does not prevent the cost or credit from resolving. A door with no qualifying cost prints no manufacturer number.

Fact.Name: Exact allocated credit for printed door rank 1
Fact.Description: Keep the selected physical door’s exact individual capped credit and its own joint payment fraction together when printing in cost order. This observation does not change the accepted aggregate door credit.

Fact.Name: Qualifying cost for printed door rank 2

Fact.Name: Manufacturer number for printed door rank 3: first four QMID characters
Fact.Description: Keep this manufacturer-number segment paired with its physical door when qualifying costs are reordered. An absent optional segment prints blank and does not prevent the cost or credit from resolving. A door with no qualifying cost prints no manufacturer number.

Fact.Description: Keep this manufacturer-number segment paired with its physical door when qualifying costs are reordered. An absent optional segment prints blank and does not prevent the cost or credit from resolving. A door with no qualifying cost prints no manufacturer number.

Fact.Name: Exact allocated credit for printed door rank 3
Fact.Description: Keep the selected physical door’s exact individual capped credit and its own joint payment fraction together when printing in cost order. This observation does not change the accepted aggregate door credit.

Fact.Name: Credit for the first printed exterior door
Fact.Description: Round the selected door’s exact capped and allocated credit once for printed line 19c. Under joint occupancy this uses the selected physical door’s payment denominator. The aggregate credit continues to use unrounded individual contributions.

Fact.Name: Total qualifying costs of the next two printed doors
Fact.Description: Add the two remaining individually entered doors after ordering their qualifying costs for the printed form.

Fact.Name: Total qualifying costs of the other printed doors
Fact.Description: Add the reordered line 19d costs and the existing qualifying itemized statement costs. These are actual costs, not amounts back-solved from the tax credit.

Fact.Name: Credit for the remaining exterior doors on the printed form
Fact.Description: For a return without positive qualifying statement-door costs, multiply the reordered actual line 19f costs by 30 percent and round once. When positive qualifying itemized doors contribute on line 19e, sum the remaining individual capped and allocated exact credits before rounding once, preserving the statutory 250 dollar limit for every physical door. An empty or zero qualifying statement uses the ordinary multiplication; an incomplete selected statement remains unresolved. A closed Section A prints zero even if unused statement details are missing. Joint household allocation on line 19h and separately rounded displayed subtotals can differ from ordinary addition; no residual or qualifying cost is invented.
